title: India International Water Week 2026 Begins: Vice-President Asks Citizens to Save Every Drop
content:
## What Happened

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan launched the 9th India International Water Week 2026 on September 22. The event is being held at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The Ministry of Jal Shakti is organising it for five days, from September 22 to 26.

This year, the focus is on “Climate Resilient Water Management.”

At the event, the Vice-President launched two new tools. One is the Sustainable Urban River Management (SURM) Framework. The other is an AI and machine learning system for managing sediment in reservoirs.

Union Minister for Jal Shakti Shri C. R. Patil and Ministers of State Shri V. Somanna and Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary were also present. Experts and delegates from India and other countries joined the programme.

## Why It Matters

India is home to about 18 per cent of the world's people. But it has only about 4 per cent of the world's freshwater. It also covers only about 2.4 per cent of the world's land area.

This means every drop counts for you and for the country.

The Vice-President said water is the base of life and of civilisations. He shared that he grew up in Tamil Nadu and saw water scarcity himself. He asked citizens to change small daily habits.

He said, “We can take a bath using two buckets or twenty buckets. The choice is ours. He also reminded people to close the tap while brushing their teeth.

He said climate change, fast urban growth and a rising population are making water management harder. He called for better river-basin management, groundwater recharge, rainwater harvesting and efficient irrigation. He also said India must move from reacting to water problems to predicting them with the help of technology.

As India works towards becoming a developed economy by 2047, he said smart and sustainable water use will be key.

## Key Points

- The Vice-President launched the SURM Framework and an AI/ML-based reservoir sediment management system.
- He said 10 inter-State agreements on water sharing have been signed so far.
- He praised the Kishau Multipurpose Project agreement among six States as a strong example of teamwork.
- He recalled his 19,000-km Ratha Yatra across Tamil Nadu, which spread awareness about river interlinking and water conservation.
- He said river interlinking can help when some regions face floods and others face drought.
- He supported the Prime Minister's call for “Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari” and urged people to make water saving a mass movement.
- He said, “Jal Suraksha will lead to Jan Suraksha and Rashtra Suraksha.”
summary: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan launched the 9th India International Water Week 2026 on September 22 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The Ministry of Jal Shakti is holding this five-day event from September 22 to 26. This year's theme is “Climate Resilient Water Management.”

title: Project Rhino Started: PM Modi Marks World Rhino Day 2026
content:
What Happened

On 22 September 2026, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi marked World Rhino Day. He praised the greater one-horned rhinoceros and thanked all those working on the front lines to protect it. He shared his message in a post on X. In the same post, he announced that Project Rhino has been started.

Why It Matters

Assam is now home to nearly 80 percent of the world's rhino population. Kaziranga's work to stop rhino poaching has earned wide appreciation. Rhinos have either come back or are well protected in parts of Bihar and West Bengal.

In Dudhwa, Uttar Pradesh, rhinos were brought back and that effort is creating history.

The Prime Minister said these results show the steady commitment of people to animal protection. Project Rhino will give money and technical support to range states. This help covers protection, habitat management, genetic improvement, and understanding of population dynamics.

The scheme aims to take species conservation forward across the country.

Key Points

- Assam now holds nearly 80 percent of the world's rhino population.
- Kaziranga's efforts to end rhino poaching have been widely appreciated.
- Rhinos have returned or are well protected in parts of Bihar and West Bengal.
- The reintroduction of rhinos in Dudhwa, Uttar Pradesh, is creating history.
- Project Rhino will support range states with funds and technical help for protection and habitat work.

## Background

World Rhino Day (22 September) raises awareness for rhino conservation; India's one-horned rhinoceros is concentrated in Assam, with Kaziranga National Park holding most of the global population.

He shared that Assam is now home to nearly 80 percent of the world's rhinos. He also announced that Project Rhino has been started to help range states protect the animal and its habitat.

title: LG of Andaman and Nicobar Islands Meets PM Modi
content:
## What Happened

On September 22, 2026, Dr. Dinesh Sharma, the Lieutenant Governor of Andaman and Nicobar Islands, met Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The Prime Minister's Office posted about the meeting on X (formerly Twitter). The post included a photo of the two leaders together.

No other details were shared. Nobody has said what the two leaders discussed. No announcement followed the meeting so far.

## What the Lieutenant Governor Does

Andaman and Nicobar Islands is a Union Territory. That means the Central Government handles many of its big decisions directly. The Lieutenant Governor is the Centre's representative on the islands.

The LG links the local administration with central ministries. So a meeting with the Prime Minister is a normal working step. It is not a rare or unusual event.

## Why Island Residents Should Note This

The islands depend on the mainland for shipping, flights, fuel, medicines and central funds. Decisions on these sit with the Centre. When the LG meets the PM, island issues can reach the top level of government.

Example: suppose families in Port Blair wait long for a specialist doctor. Or a trader in Car Nicobar waits weeks for a shipping slot. Fixing such problems usually starts with a policy or funding call in Delhi. Meetings like this are one route for those matters to travel.

But be clear: no one has said this meeting covered any such subject. Do not assume it did.

## How to Follow What Comes Next

If you want to know what happens after such a meeting, use official channels only:

1. Check the Press Information Bureau at pib.gov.in for official releases.
2. Follow the Prime Minister's Office and pmindia.gov.in for announcements.
3. Use india.gov.in for Union Territory information.
4. Watch the Andaman and Nicobar Islands administration for any local follow-up.
5. Treat social media claims carefully. Wait for an official statement before believing them.

A meeting alone does not change any rule, scheme or fee. A change is real only when a written order or official release says so.

## Who This Applies To

This news matters mainly to people living in or doing business in Andaman and Nicobar Islands. It also matters to anyone tracking how the Centre works with Union Territories.

## Key Points

- Dr. Dinesh Sharma is the Lieutenant Governor of Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
- He met Prime Minister Narendra Modi on September 22, 2026.
- The PMO shared the news on X with a photo.
- The meeting was a formal one.
- No further information was given by the source.

This win gives India its first Gold medal at this edition of the Asian Games. It is a big moment for Indian cricket and for every fan back home. The Prime Minister said the team has made the nation proud.

The win can inspire many young cricketers across the country. If you are a young player, this shows what focus and teamwork can achieve on a world stage.

Girls' cricket has spread across many states, so there are more teams and trials than before. Check the official portal for the latest rules.

What Happened

On 22 September 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated Suchika Tariyal. She won a Bronze medal in Mixed Martial Arts at the Asian Games. Her win gave India its first ever Asian Games medal in this sport.

The Prime Minister's Office shared his message on X the same day.

Why It Matters

Mixed Martial Arts is still a new sport for India on the world stage. No Indian athlete had ever reached the Asian Games podium in this event before. This medal shows that Indian fighters can compete with the best in tough, contact sports.

It also gives young athletes in India a new dream to chase.

Why It Matters

The Prime Minister called the win a historic achievement for the country. He said her dedication and zeal stand out. He also wished her many more successes in the coming years.

Key Points

- Suchika Tariyal won Bronze in Mixed Martial Arts at the Asian Games.
- This is India's first ever Asian Games medal in Mixed Martial Arts.
- PM Narendra Modi congratulated her on 22 September 2026.
- He called the win a historic achievement for India.

## What a First Medal Changes for the Sport

A first medal in any sport changes how people look at it. Mixed Martial Arts had no Indian name on the Asian Games podium before this. Now it has one.

Medals often bring more attention from sports bodies, coaches and sponsors. Training centres in that sport get easier to justify. Talent hunts also start looking in new places.

For a young athlete, the path looks less risky now. Parents who once asked where an MMA career leads have a result to look at.

This does not mean the sport becomes easy overnight. India still needs more gyms, more qualified coaches and more regular competitions at district and state level.

## If You Want to Try Mixed Martial Arts

Mixed Martial Arts mixes striking and grappling. Most people enter it through a base sport first. Here is a simple way to start.

- Pick one base sport to begin with: boxing, wrestling, judo, taekwondo or muay thai.
- Join a gym with a qualified coach. Ask about safety rules, medical cover and how sparring is supervised.
- Build fitness step by step. Strength, stamina and mobility matter as much as technique.
- Enter district and state level bouts to get real match experience.
- Keep your age proof and medical fitness records ready for competitions.
- For recognised training centres and athlete support, check the Sports Authority of India and your state sports council.

Parents and athletes should also ask about injury cover and recovery time. Contact sports need careful, supervised training.

title: e-PAN Card: Get Your Digital PAN Free in 5-10 Minutes
content:
## What Happened

The Income Tax Department issues a digital version of your PAN card. This digital card is called e-PAN. It comes as a PDF file that you can save on your phone or computer. It has the same legal value as the plastic PAN card.

So you can use it for banking, investments and tax filing.

Every e-PAN carries a QR code. That code holds your name, PAN number, date of birth and photo. Anyone can scan it to check that your card is genuine.

The government also approved the PAN 2.0 plan. About Rs 1,435 crore has been set aside for it. Under this plan, new PAN cards will carry a QR code.

Your old PAN card will still work. You do not have to replace it.

## Who Is Eligible

You need three things to get a free e-PAN. You must have a valid Aadhaar number. Your mobile number must be linked to that Aadhaar, because you need it for the OTP. And you must not already have a PAN.

Some people cannot apply. Minors below 18 years cannot apply. Anyone who already has a PAN will not get a second one.

If your mobile is not linked to Aadhaar, link it first at [aadhaar.gov.in](https://aadhaar.gov.in) or at an Aadhaar centre.

## Benefits

The instant e-PAN is completely free. The department charges you nothing for it. It is generated in about 5-10 minutes.

A download link lands in your email, and you can open it from anywhere.

The physical PAN card works differently. It takes 15-20 working days to reach you. You also pay a fee of about Rs 107 for it.

The e-PAN is valid for your whole life. You never have to renew it. It works in almost every situation, from banks to tax filing.

## How to Apply

Step 1: Open the Income Tax e-Filing portal at [incometax.gov.in](https://incometax.gov.in).

Step 2: Click the Instant e-PAN section on the homepage.

Step 3: Choose Get New e-PAN.

Step 4: Enter your 12-digit Aadhaar number. Type only the 12 digits. Do not add dashes or spaces.

Step 5: An OTP will reach your Aadhaar-linked mobile. Verify it. If your mobile is not linked, update your Aadhaar first.

Step 6: Pick your date of birth proof from DigiLocker. You can also verify the date of birth yourself.

Step 7: Submit the form. You will get an acknowledgement number. Note it down safely.

Step 8: Within 5-10 minutes, a PDF download link reaches your email. Download it and save it.

## How to Download an Existing PAN

If you already have a PAN and want a copy, go to [incometax.gov.in](https://incometax.gov.in). Open the Reprint PAN Card section. Enter your PAN number and Aadhaar number.

Pay a fee of about Rs 50. Your physical card will arrive in 15-20 working days. You can also download a digital copy from DigiLocker, which is equally valid.

## Watch Out For Scam Emails

The government has warned about fake emails going around. These emails say your PAN has expired and ask you to update it through a link. The Income Tax Department never asks for your personal details over email.

Never click such links and never enter your PAN details there.

If you see a suspicious email, do not click it. Check everything only on the official portal. You can report it at webmanager@incometax.gov.in.

Download the e-PAN only through official apps like mAadhaar and DigiLocker.

## Important Dates

The PAN 2.0 update was approved with a budget of Rs 1,435 crore. The year 2026 is mentioned for this plan. No exact date is given in the official source.

title: CKYC 2.0: One KYC for All Your Financial Products
content:
## What Happened

CKYC 2.0 started rolling out on August 1, 2026. CKYC stands for Central Know Your Customer. It is one central system built for India's financial sector.

Earlier, every bank, mutual fund, and insurance company did its own KYC. You had to submit the same papers again and again. Under CKYC, your details are verified once and stored in a central registry.

CERSAI manages this registry. CERSAI is the Central Registry of Securitisation Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest of India. It works under the RBI and is the most trusted source for KYC records.

## What Is New In CKYC 2.0

- OTP-based consent: You no longer need to hand over physical documents. One OTP is enough to give your consent.
- 14-digit CKYC identifier: This is a unique number given to you. Share it to onboard with any financial product.
- Confidence score: Every KYC record gets a score that shows how verified it is.
- Digital-first approach: Everything moves online, so paperwork drops.

## Who Can Get CKYC

Any person who wants a CKYC record must go through a regulated financial institution. Banks, mutual fund companies, and insurance companies can all do this for you. You cannot create the record on your own.

## Benefits

- You do not submit the same documents again and again. Do KYC once and use it everywhere.
- Opening a new account or investment becomes faster.
- One record covers all your financial products, including bank, mutual fund, and insurance.
- Your record sits in one secure central place.
- A central system lowers the risk of fraud.

## CKYC vs eKYC vs Normal KYC

- CKYC: Your data is stored in CERSAI's registry. Any financial institution can access it only after taking your permission.
- eKYC: This is Aadhaar-based digital verification. It happens in real time when you apply for a financial product.
- Normal KYC: You carry physical papers like PAN, Aadhaar, and address proof to the institution. They check the papers and keep the record.

## How to Register

1. Visit any regulated financial institution, such as a bank, mutual fund, or insurance company.
2. Submit the needed documents like PAN, Aadhaar, and a photo.
3. The institution verifies them and uploads them to CERSAI.
4. You receive a 14-digit CKYC identifier.
5. Use this number for fast onboarding at any other financial institution.

## How to Check Your CKYC Status

1. Open the CERSAI website at [cersai.org.in](https://cersai.org.in).
2. Go to the CKYC Status Check section.
3. Enter your 14-digit CKYC number or your PAN number.
4. Your status will show on the screen.

If you did CKYC earlier and forgot your number, contact your bank or financial institution. They can share your CKYC number with you.

title: SEBI Issues Order on Omaxe Limited Over Minimum Public Shareholding Rule
content:
What Happened SEBI has issued an order about Omaxe Limited. The order is about the company not meeting the minimum public shareholding rule. SEBI shared the order on its website on 24 September 2026.

The public note only carries the title of the order. It does not explain what action SEBI has taken.

What Changes The order is part of SEBI's enforcement work against listed companies. A listed company must keep a set share of its stock with the public. If it fails to do so, SEBI can step in.

This order deals with that failure for Omaxe Limited. The release does not spell out any penalty, timeline, or remedy.

What You Need to Do If you hold shares in Omaxe Limited, read the full order on the SEBI website. If you do not hold any shares, this order does not need any action from you. Do not act on forwarded messages about this order.

Always check the official SEBI page for facts.

Deadline The release does not mention any deadline. The order was published on 24 September 2026.

## What Minimum Public Shareholding Means in Plain Words

SEBI's minimum public shareholding rule says a listed company must keep a set portion of its shares with the public.

Public means ordinary investors, not promoters or promoter group. The exact portion is fixed in SEBI's rules and the SCRR. You can read the current rule on sebi.gov.in.

When the public float is too small, a few large holders control most of the stock. That can mean:

- Fewer shares available to buy or sell on the exchange.
- Sharper price swings when someone trades a big quantity.
- Less room for outside investors to have a real say.

That is why SEBI tracks this rule closely. An order like the Omaxe one means the regulator found a gap.

To check any listed company, open its latest shareholding pattern. Companies file this every quarter with BSE and NSE. Look at the promoter and public holding split in that table.

## Practical Steps If You Hold Omaxe Shares

1. Read the full order, not the headline. Open the Enforcement section of sebi.gov.in and search for Omaxe. The order is dated 24 September 2026.
2. Check the latest shareholding pattern. BSE and NSE carry it under the company's name. Note the promoter holding and the public holding.
3. Watch company announcements. A listed company must inform the exchanges about material developments. Check the Omaxe page on both exchanges.
4. Ignore WhatsApp and Telegram forwards about this order. People often mix new orders with old news.
5. If your holding is large for your income, speak to a SEBI-registered investment adviser.

Any remedy, penalty or deadline will sit inside the order document itself. The short public release does not carry those details.

For a general sense of how such orders work: SEBI looks into a possible breach, gives the company a chance to respond, and then passes an order. The order usually states the directions and the time allowed to appeal.
summary: SEBI has passed an order in the matter of non-compliance of minimum public shareholding in Omaxe Limited. The order was published on 24 September 2026. The official release does not give details of the penalty or the next steps.

title: PM Modi Sends Ayurveda Day Wishes, Calls Ayurveda a Way of Healthy Living
content:
## What Happened

On 23 September 2026, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi extended warm greetings to all citizens on Ayurveda Day. He shared his message on X, the social media platform. In it, he said Ayurveda is not merely a system of treatment.

He called it a powerful medium for a healthy and balanced lifestyle. He asked every Indian to strengthen their resolve to embrace this rich heritage. Along with the message, he also posted a Sanskrit Subhashitam on the holistic nature of Ayurveda.

## Why It Matters

Ayurveda is one of India's oldest systems of medicine. It looks at the whole person, not just the disease. It links your daily habits to your overall health.

That is the idea the PM wanted to highlight on this day.

The Sanskrit verse he shared explains this clearly. It says Ayurveda is the science that tells you which habits help you and which harm you. It also speaks about what makes life happy or unhappy, and what separates a healthy life from a diseased one.

Most importantly, it talks about how to live long and well. It discusses the nature and measure of a person's lifespan. In simple words, the verse asks you to think about your everyday routine, not just your medicines.

## Key Points

- PM Modi greeted all citizens with warm wishes on Ayurveda Day.
- He said Ayurveda is more than a treatment system, it is a way of living well.
- He shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam on X to explain the true meaning of Ayurveda.
- The verse says Ayurveda covers helpful and harmful habits, happy and sad life, and lifespan.
- He urged people to renew their commitment to this rich heritage.

## What You Can Do

You can read the PM's full post on X. You can also learn one small healthy habit from Ayurveda and try it in your daily routine. Small steps towards balance can make a big difference over time.

## Simple Ayurveda Habits You Can Start Today

Ayurveda gives a lot of weight to daily routine. It calls this dinacharya. The idea is simple: your habits shape your health over the years.

Two people with the same problem may get different advice. That is because Ayurveda looks at your body type, your food and the season together. A doctor decides what suits you.

Some general habits you can try:

- Wake up and sleep at roughly the same time daily.
- Eat your main meal at a fixed time.
- Choose freshly cooked home food over packaged snacks.
- Take a short walk after meals, if your doctor allows.
- Avoid heavy, oily food close to bedtime.
- Spend a few minutes on deep breathing or light stretching.

These are general wellness steps. They do not replace medical treatment. If you have a health condition, ask your doctor first.

## How to Find a Genuine Ayurveda Doctor

Ayurveda is a recognised medical system in India and it is regulated. So you can check who is qualified.

- Look for a BAMS degree from a recognised Ayurveda college.
- Confirm the doctor is registered with a state medical council.
- Government AYUSH health and wellness centres offer Ayurveda services in many districts.
- Do not buy strong Ayurveda medicines online without a prescription.
- Tell your Ayurveda doctor about every other medicine you take.

The Ministry of AYUSH runs the official portal for schemes, colleges and advisories. Government research councils share study updates on the AYUSH research portal. Check the official portal for the latest rules.
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi greeted all Indians on Ayurveda Day with a warm message. He said Ayurveda is not just a way to treat illness, but a strong path to a healthy and balanced life. He also shared a Sanskrit verse on X to explain what Ayurveda truly means.

title: NRAA Reviews Draft Watershed Guidelines Under REWARD Programme
content:
## What Happened

The National Rainfed Area Authority (NRAA) held a National Level Technical Committee (NLTC) meeting on 22 September 2026. The venue was the NASC Complex in New Delhi. The meeting took place under the REWARD programme, which works on improving watersheds for farming.

Dr. Chandra Shekhar Kumar, CEO of NRAA, led the meeting. Dr. A. K. Nayak from ICAR, Shri Nitin Khade from the Department of Land Resources, and officials from Odisha and Karnataka also joined. Scientists, state nodal agency teams, technical partners, NGOs and the REWARD project team took part.

Around 45 people attended in total. Dr. Susama Sudhishri coordinated the session.

## Why It Matters

Watersheds decide how well rain-fed farms store water and stay productive. The draft National Technical Guidelines (NTG) will guide future watershed work across India under Watershed Development Component - Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana 3.0. So the decisions taken here can affect farmers in many states.

The CEO asked for proof behind every claim made in the draft guidelines. He used data from the REWARD programme as the base. He also told Odisha and Karnataka to share their watershed data and Decision Support System with all stakeholders.

Dr. A. K. Nayak pushed for linking Land Resource Inventory with hydrology for better planning. Officials also discussed finishing project reports faster and building web portals soon.

## Key Points

- NRAA held the National Level Technical Committee meeting on 22 September 2026 at NASC Complex, New Delhi.
- Around 45 participants joined, including officials from Odisha and Karnataka.
- Members reviewed the additions made in the second draft of the National Technical Guidelines.
- The CEO asked states to share watershed data and the Decision Support System with all stakeholders.
- A suggestion was made to cut project report preparation time from 6 months to 3 months.
- The final guidelines will support watershed development under PMKSY 3.0.

## What State Agencies and Partners Should Track Now

The second draft is still under review. Final guidelines are not out yet.

- State nodal agencies can keep watershed data ready.
- Odisha and Karnataka were asked to share watershed data and the Decision Support System.
- Project report teams may prepare for a faster timeline. A suggestion was made to cut report preparation time from 6 months to 3 months.
- Farmers in project areas can ask their local agriculture office about upcoming watershed work.

Check the official portal for the latest rules.

## How Better Watershed Planning Reaches the Farm

Watersheds decide how rain-fed farms store water and handle dry spells. Better planning can help farmers plan crops and water use.

- Linking Land Resource Inventory with hydrology can help planners match water structures to local land.
- Faster project reports can help projects start sooner, if the suggestion is accepted.
- The final guidelines will guide watershed work under PMKSY 3.0.
- No farmer-level application window is announced in this update. Contact your state nodal agency or local agriculture office for area-specific details.

Check the official portal for the latest rules.
summary: The National Rainfed Area Authority held a National Level Technical Committee meeting on 22 September 2026 in New Delhi. About 45 experts reviewed the second draft of the National Technical Guidelines under the REWARD programme. These guidelines will shape future watershed development work under PMKSY 3.0.

title: EPFO Citizen's Charter: What It Means for You
content:
## What Happened

The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has published its official Citizen's Charter, a comprehensive document that outlines the organization's commitment to service delivery standards, timelines, and grievance redressal mechanisms for subscribers and employers.

The Citizen's Charter serves as a public accountability framework, detailing the specific services EPFO provides, the maximum timeframes for service delivery, and the quality standards subscribers can expect when interacting with EPFO offices.

## Key Services Covered in the Charter

The EPFO Citizen's Charter covers the following critical service areas:

**For Subscribers:**
- Universal Account Number (UAN) generation and activation
- KYC seeding and updation (Aadhaar, PAN, Bank details)
- Online claim settlement (Form 19, 10C, 31)
- PF transfer requests between employers
- Pension Payment Order (PPO) generation for EPS retirees
- Life Certificate submission and pension continuation

**For Employers:**
- New establishment registration and code allotment
- Monthly ECR (Electronic Challan cum Return) processing
- Digital signature certificate registration
- Exemption applications for PF Trust formation

## Service Delivery Timelines

The Charter specifies maximum processing times for each service:

- UAN Generation: Within 48 hours of KYC approval
- Online Claim Settlement: Within 20 working days
- PF Transfer Requests: Within 20 working days
- Grievance Redressal (EPFiGMS): Initial response within 7 days, resolution within 30 days
- Joint Declaration (Name/Date corrections): Within 30 working days

## Grievance Redressal Mechanism

The Charter establishes a three-tier grievance redressal structure:

1. **First Level**: Regional PF Commissioner at the concerned Regional Office
2. **Second Level**: Additional Central PF Commissioner at Zonal Office
3. **Third Level**: Central PF Commissioner at EPFO Headquarters

Subscribers can file grievances online through EPFiGMS (epfigms.gov.in), CPGRAMS (pgportal.gov.in), or by visiting the concerned EPFO office in person.

## Why It Matters

The Citizen's Charter empowers subscribers by providing transparent service standards and accountability mechanisms. It ensures that EPFO services are delivered within defined timelines and provides clear escalation paths when service delivery falls short of commitments.

For employers, the Charter clarifies compliance requirements and reduces uncertainty around registration, challan processing, and statutory obligations.

## Key Points

- EPFO's Citizen's Charter defines service standards, timelines, and grievance mechanisms
- Online claims must be settled within 20 working days as per Charter commitments
- Three-tier grievance redressal: Regional → Zonal → Headquarters level
- UAN generation guaranteed within 48 hours of successful KYC verification
- Charter applies uniformly across all 138+ EPFO Regional Offices nationwide

title: DGFT's Policy Relaxation Committee: What the Official Source Tells You
content:
## What Happened

DGFT maintains a Policy Relaxation Committee. DGFT is the Directorate General of Foreign Trade. It works under the Ministry of Commerce & Industry.

DGFT has not published the committee's mandate in detail. It has not listed members, meeting dates, minutes or past decisions. There is also no published application form, fee or deadline.

India's trade rules are set by the Foreign Trade Policy and the Handbook of Procedures. Those documents are where any relaxation clause would normally appear. So far, DGFT has not spelled out how this committee fits into that chain.

Trade rules are written for the general case. Your case may not fit.

This matters most to exporters and importers who hold an IEC and a DGFT licence — an Advance Authorisation, EPCG, DFIA, or an import licence naming a specific product code. It also matters to any unit that must meet an export obligation inside a fixed window.

Say you run a small export unit in Tiruppur. Your buyer cancels an order, and your Advance Authorisation export obligation window closes before you can ship. Or an importer's licence names one product code, while customs clears goods under a slightly different one. In such situations, a business wants a route to ask for relief.

A committee with "relaxation" in its name is normally where such requests land. But relief is never automatic. It usually needs a written request, supporting papers and an official decision. Since DGFT has not published the process here, do not assume a fixed route exists.

## Key Points

- The Policy Relaxation Committee sits under DGFT.
- DGFT is part of the Ministry of Commerce & Industry.
- The committee's members are not published.
- No meeting schedule, fee or deadline is published.
- No application method is published.
- Hardship claims still need a strong paper trail.
- Any relief, if granted, applies to that case alone. It does not change the rule for other traders.

## Papers That Help Your Case

Keep these ready before you write to anyone:

- Your IEC and the licence or authorisation in question.
- Shipping bills, bills of entry and bank realisation certificates.
- Buyer or supplier emails, cancellation notes and contracts.
- Any public notice or notification that touches your case.
- A short covering letter: which rule blocks you, what relief you want, and why your case does not fit the general rule.

## What You Can Do Now

1. Pin down the exact rule blocking you. Note the paragraph number in the Foreign Trade Policy or Handbook of Procedures, plus any related public notice.
2. Build a file: IEC, licences, shipping bills, bank realisation certificates, and emails with your buyer or supplier.
3. Approach your Regional Authority (RA) of DGFT first. Ask in writing whether your case can be considered for relaxation, and under which provision.
4. Check the DGFT website and its public notices regularly. Any new committee process would show up there first.
5. Keep your trade plans on rules that are already published. Do not hold back a shipment assuming relief will arrive in time.
6. Treat agents carefully. Nobody can promise a relaxation when no published process exists. Confirm every step with your RA or a trade expert.

Example: an exporter whose shipping bill description does not match the licence can write to the RA, attach both documents, and ask what correction route applies. That letter creates a record, even if the answer is no.

Confirm your own licence conditions with your RA, and get any assurance in writing. Check the official portal for the latest rules.
summary: The Policy Relaxation Committee is a DGFT body that deals with requests for relief when a trade case does not fit the general rule. DGFT has not published its members, process, fees or deadlines, so route any request in writing through your Regional Authority.

title: DPIIT Recognition for Startups: What It Means for You
content:
## What Happened

DPIIT stands for the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade. It works under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

DPIIT recognition is a certificate that marks a young company as a recognised startup under the Startup India initiative. Once approved, your company gets a recognition number.

That number is useful when you deal with government schemes, banks, incubators and investors. Founders chase it because doors open more easily with it in hand.

The Startup India programme runs this process. You apply yourself, and DPIIT decides based on the current framework.

## Who Is Eligible

Two things matter most: your business structure, and how far your business has already grown.

Broadly, founders apply as a private limited company, a registered partnership firm, or a limited liability partnership. A sole proprietorship usually does not fit as it is.

Your business should still be in its early stage. You should have a product, service or idea that can grow, create jobs, or solve a real problem.

The exact rules are set by DPIIT and updated from time to time. Check your own case on https://www.startupindia.gov.in/content/sih/en/startup-scheme.html before you file.

## What the Recognition Gives You

Different departments treat a recognised startup differently. In practice, founders go for this tag because it helps with:

- Startup India schemes and funding programmes.
- Tax-related benefits, which have their own separate conditions and approvals.
- Easier conversations with banks, incubators and accelerators.
- A recognised tag during tenders and investor talks.

Being listed for a benefit does not mean you get it automatically. Each one has its own rules and its own application.

## How a Founder Gets Recognised

1. Register your business first. Many founders also complete Udyam registration at https://udyamregistration.gov.in/.
2. Create an account on https://www.startupindia.gov.in/ using your company details and email.
3. Fill the recognition form. You describe your startup, product, team and current stage.
4. Upload the papers the form asks for.
5. Submit and track it. You receive a recognition number once approved.

## Papers and Details to Keep Ready

Keep these handy before you start:

- Certificate of incorporation or partnership registration.
- PAN of the business entity.
- Names and details of directors or partners.
- A short write-up on what your startup actually does.
- Website or app links, if you have them.
- Details of any funding received so far.

The exact list depends on your entity type. Check the official portal for the latest rules.

## Timeline and Deadlines

There is no fixed deadline to apply. You can file once your business is registered and you meet the current conditions.

Approval time varies from case to case. Do not put your other filings on hold for it.

## A Real Example

Sneha runs a small software company in Pune. She had a private limited company and had also completed Udyam registration. She applied for DPIIT recognition, got her number, and used it while applying for a government scheme and while talking to an angel investor.

Her friend Rohit was a sole proprietor. He checked the rules first and found he needed to change his entity type before applying. Names here are only illustrative.

## What to Do Next

1. Confirm your entity type and growth stage fit the current framework.
2. Keep your registration papers, PAN and business details ready.
3. Apply only through the official Startup India portal.
4. Never pay an agent for a guaranteed recognition. No such guarantee exists.
5. Check the official portal for the latest rules.

title: DGFT Page on Import, Export and SCOMET Policy: A Simple Guide for Traders
content:
## What Happened

DGFT is the government body that writes and enforces India's rules for goods crossing the border. It works under the Ministry of Commerce & Industry.

Two things decide most shipments: the Foreign Trade Policy, and the ITC(HS) code that classifies your product. SCOMET is the separate list for sensitive goods — special chemicals, organisms, materials, equipment and technologies.

No new notification, fee or form has been announced. Nothing in the import-export or SCOMET rules changed on that account. Your current paperwork and authorisations stay valid until DGFT issues a separate notification.

## What Changes

No existing rule has been altered. No new deadline and no new charge. Your current paperwork stays valid.

Treat this as a signpost, not a fresh order. If a rule change comes later, DGFT will publish it separately as its own notification.

Who this applies to: importers, exporters, customs brokers, freight forwarders and manufacturers who buy or sell abroad. Exporters of chemicals, electronics, defence-linked parts, biotech material and encryption software should watch SCOMET closely.

If your product is not on the SCOMET list, your routine does not change at all. If it is, the authorisation requirement that already exists continues to apply.

## What You Need to Do

1. Get your Importer-Exporter Code (IEC) in place. Almost every commercial shipment needs it.
2. Find the correct ITC(HS) code for your product. This decides duty, and it decides whether SCOMET applies.
3. Match your code against the current SCOMET list. If your item is covered, you normally need an export authorisation before you ship.
4. Keep your papers ready: commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or airway bill, letter of credit where used, purchase order and shipping bill.
5. File the shipping bill or bill of entry through customs, and keep copies of every clearance.
6. If anything is unclear, ask your customs broker or a trade consultant before booking cargo.

For a SCOMET item, the authorisation must be in hand before the cargo moves. Do not book freight on the assumption that clearance will come through in time.

Example: A Pune firm exporting a specialty chemical to a buyer in Germany finds its product inside a SCOMET category. It applies for an authorisation, waits for clearance, and only then books cargo. A second firm exporting plain cotton fabric needs no such clearance — it files the shipping bill with the right ITC(HS) code and moves on.

## Deadline

Not specified. No date has been announced. Check the official portal for the latest rules.
summary: DGFT runs India's import-export rules and the SCOMET list for sensitive goods; no rule, fee or deadline has changed, so existing paperwork stays valid. Check your ITC(HS) code and confirm whether SCOMET authorisation applies before you ship.

title: SEBI Issues Release Order Against Rashesh Purohit in TV Vision Limited Case
content:
## What Happened

SEBI has published a release order naming Rashesh Purohit as a defaulter in the matter of TV Vision Limited. The case sits under Certificate No. 7475 of 2023. He is identified by PAN ADQPP1270Q. The notice carries the date 24 September 2026 and belongs to SEBI's recovery proceedings.

A release order in a recovery case is a formal record that dues linked to that case remain unpaid. The person's name, PAN and certificate number are published so anyone checking can identify the exact individual.

## What Changes

Once a person is marked a defaulter in a recovery matter, the name enters SEBI's public defaulter records. Recovery can then move ahead — attaching bank accounts, demat accounts or property to recover the dues.

SEBI's order does not state the amount involved and does not list the current stage of recovery. Nobody else's rights change because of this notice. It names one individual, not TV Vision Limited.

## What You Need to Do

If you have no link to this case, no action is needed. The notice does not apply to the general public or to ordinary investors.

If you are the person named, or you manage accounts for that person:

- Get the full order copy using Certificate No. 7475 of 2023 and PAN ADQPP1270Q.
- Note the stage of recovery and any response date printed on the notice served on you.
- Reply in writing through a securities lawyer before that date.
- Do not ignore letters sent to your registered address.

Details you need ready: your PAN, the certificate number, and ID plus address proof if you write to SEBI.

## Deadline

SEBI's order does not give a deadline. Time limits for replying to a recovery notice usually appear in the notice served on the person named. Confirm the exact date with SEBI or with a securities lawyer.

## What a Defaulter Tag Means in Recovery Cases

A recovery case moves in stages. SEBI passes an order, then a demand notice goes out. If the dues stay unpaid, the person is marked a defaulter. After that, bank accounts, demat accounts or property can be attached. The person named can still pay or settle the dues.

Example: two people may share the name Rashesh Purohit. If your PAN is different from ADQPP1270Q, the listing is not about you.

## How to Check Whether You Are on the Defaulter List

Go to sebi.gov.in, then enforcement, then recovery proceedings. Match the full name and the PAN together.

- PAN different from ADQPP1270Q — the order is not about you.
- PAN matches — read the full order before acting.
- Listing looks wrong — write to SEBI with your PAN and ID proof.

Shareholders of TV Vision Limited need not act on this order. It names an individual. Check the official portal for the latest rules.

title: IMEI Tampering Can Land You in Jail: A Simple Guide to India's Telecom Device Rules
content:
## What Happened

India runs one of the world's largest mobile networks. In July 2026, the country had 1,204.01 million active wireless mobile subscribers. Crores of people use phones for payments, government services and daily work.

Every phone carries an IMEI. It is a unique 15-digit number that identifies your device on a telecom network. Tamper with it, and your phone turns fake or blocked on the network.

Because so much depends on these devices, the government wants every phone on the network to be genuine. The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has explained its rules on IMEI numbers for owners, buyers, sellers and makers.

## What Changes

Tampering with an IMEI is now unlawful under the Telecommunications Act, 2023. It is a crime if you intentionally remove, erase, change or alter a device's unique Mobile Device Equipment Identification number.

It is also a crime to make, use, sell, traffic in, control, keep or possess hardware or software that you know can change an IMEI.

The punishment is serious. Up to 3 years in jail, a fine of up to ₹50 lakh, or both. These offences are cognizable and non-bailable under Section 42(7).

Anyone who helps or encourages the crime faces the same punishment under Section 42(6). Section 42(3)(e) also bans getting SIM cards through fraud, cheating or impersonation.

The rules cover phone owners, buyers, second-hand dealers, repair shops, manufacturers, importers, brand owners and anyone using a SIM card.

## What You Need to Do

Know your IMEI. Dial *#06# on your handset and the 15-digit number shows on screen. A dual-SIM phone usually has two IMEI numbers, one for each SIM slot.

Check the TAC. The first eight digits of an IMEI form the Type Allocation Code. It tells you the device model. The Global System for Mobile Communications Association (GSMA) gives out TACs to manufacturers.

Verify your device. Visit the Sanchar Saathi portal or mobile app. You can also send KYM <15-digit IMEI number> by SMS to 14422.

If you make devices, register first. Manufacturers must register IMEIs of telecom devices made in India before the first sale, testing, research or other use. Do this on the Device Setu–Indian Counterfeited Device Restriction (ICDR) portal. Devices must carry valid, unique and untampered IMEIs.

If you import devices, register the IMEIs with the Central Government before the devices enter India, on the Device Setu–ICDR portal. Imported devices must carry valid and authorised IMEIs.

If you sell devices, check every IMEI. Resellers and retailers must offer only devices with valid and untampered IMEIs. If you deal in used phones, check the IMEI against the government's central database of tampered and blacklisted devices before you close the deal. You pay a small fee for each IMEI check. Selling tampered or configurable IMEIs can bring strict legal action.

If you own a brand, register it on the Device Setu–ICDR portal and link it to the right GSMA Type Allocation Code. Devices sold under the brand must carry authentic and authorised IMEIs and follow cybersecurity rules.

## What Citizens Should Avoid

Do not use, buy or put together devices like modems, modules or SIM boxes with tampered or configurable IMEIs.

Do not get a SIM card using fake documents, fraud, cheating or impersonation.

Do not transfer, sell or hand over a SIM card issued in your name to someone else. They may misuse it.

Do not use apps, websites or any other method to change your Calling Line Identity (CLI) or other telecom identifiers.

## What Citizens Should Do

Buy mobile devices only from authorised sellers, and verify the IMEI details.

Protect your phone with a strong password, PIN or biometric lock.

Get your phone repaired only at authorised service centres. This lowers the risk of IMEI tampering.

Here is a real example. A second-hand shop offers to "rewrite" the IMEI of a blocked phone so it works again. If you agree, you are breaking the law, and so is the shop. Jail, fine or both can follow.

If your phone is lost or stolen, act step by step. First, file a report with your local police and keep a copy of the complaint.

Next, get a duplicate SIM card for the lost number from your telecom operator. Under TRAI rules, SMS services stay blocked for the first 24 hours after a re-issued SIM is activated. Sanchar Saathi needs a mobile OTP, so wait 24 hours before you apply.

Then register the blocking request on the Sanchar Saathi (CEIR) portal or mobile app. Upload the police report and a valid ID proof. You will get a unique Request ID.

If you later get your device back, tell the local police first. Then use your Request ID on the portal to unblock the handset safely.

## Deadline

No deadline applies. These rules are already in force, so follow them right away.

Keep these links handy: https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2313715 | https://sancharsaathi.gov.in/ | https://www.dot.gov.in/

Check the official portal for the latest rules.
summary: India treats IMEI tampering as a crime under the Telecommunications Act, 2023, with up to 3 years in jail, a ₹50 lakh fine, or both. Verify your IMEI, buy from authorised sellers, and use Sanchar Saathi if your phone is lost.

title: DPIIT Startup Recognition Guidelines: What Young Companies Should Know
content:
## What Happened
DPIIT — the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade — has issued revised guidelines for startup recognition. DPIIT works under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. Startup recognition is the official tag that tells the government a young company counts as a startup.

The revised guidelines set out how that tag is granted, and what a young company must show to get it. They replace the earlier set of rules. If you applied under the old rules, re-check whether you still qualify.

## What Changes
Recognition matters in practice. Many government schemes, tenders and benefit programmes ask for a recognised startup number before they let you apply. A company without the tag is treated as an ordinary business.

The revised guidelines tighten and clarify the conditions a company must meet. They look at your entity type, how old your entity is, and whether your work is innovative or scalable. Check startupindia.gov.in for the current conditions.

## Who It Applies To
- Private limited companies, registered partnerships and LLPs.
- Companies in their early years of operation, where the founders are still building.
- Businesses working on a product, service or process that can scale.
- Founders already registered on the Udyam MSME portal. Many register there first, then apply for startup recognition.

Individuals, sole proprietorships and unregistered firms generally cannot apply. Register your entity first.

## What You Need to Do
1. Register your company or LLP, and keep the certificate of incorporation safe.
2. Create an account on the Startup India portal.
3. Fill the recognition form: entity name, registration number, date of incorporation, and details of founders, directors or partners.
4. Explain what your business does, and why it is innovative or scalable.
5. Upload the papers the portal asks for. These usually include the certificate of incorporation, PAN and director or partner details.
6. Submit the form and save your application number for follow-up.

Keep these ready before you start: certificate of incorporation, PAN, names and details of directors or partners, and a short write-up on your product.

Use the exact name printed on your certificate of incorporation, not your brand name. A mismatched name or a wrong date of incorporation is the most common reason an application comes back.

Example: suppose you registered a private limited company on 25 March 2026 and started selling online. You have not filed your first annual return yet. You can still apply, because recognition is about your entity and your idea, not your revenue.

## Deadline
No closing date is listed for applying. Applications are open through the Startup India portal, and the rules can change. Confirm the current position before you file. Check the official portal for the latest rules: https://www.startupindia.gov.in/ and https://udyamregistration.gov.in/.

title: Income Tax Exemption Notifications for Startups: A Simple Guide
content:
## What Happened

Startup India, run by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) under the Ministry of Commerce & Industry, has issued income tax exemption notifications for startups. These are official government orders, not news reports or opinions. Each notification says which startups can claim an exemption and on what terms.

In plain terms, an exemption notification is a government order that allows an eligible startup to skip income tax on its profits for a fixed period. If you run a DPIIT-recognised startup, these orders decide whether your profits can escape income tax for that set period. Most founders come across them while filing returns or planning the next financial year.

Who this applies to: private limited companies and LLPs that hold DPIIT recognition. A regular shop, trader or plain MSME does not qualify through this route. Sole proprietorships and ordinary partnership firms usually sit outside the startup recognition route too.

## What Changes

All startup-linked tax exemption notifications now sit together on the Startup India portal. Earlier, founders had to hunt across several government websites for each order. Now the exemption orders, the application route through the Inter-Ministerial Board (IMB) and related updates are grouped at startupindia.gov.in.

Businesses registered on Udyam (udyamregistration.gov.in) should note one thing. MSME registration and DPIIT startup recognition are two different things. One does not automatically give you the other.

How it works: you first hold valid DPIIT recognition. You then apply to the Inter-Ministerial Board, which reviews your business activity, innovation angle and records. Only after that route do you claim the exemption while filing your return. Nothing here is automatic.

The exact tax amounts, the number of eligible years and the conditions are not spelled out in every notice. Read each notification in full before you assume anything applies to you.

## What You Need to Do

1. Confirm your startup holds valid DPIIT recognition. Without it, these exemptions generally will not apply.
2. Keep your certificate of incorporation, PAN and startup recognition details handy.
3. Go through the notifications and check whether your business activity and incorporation date fall inside the stated window.
4. If your case fits, apply through the Inter-Ministerial Board route on startupindia.gov.in, with your recognition certificate and financial statements ready.
5. Share the notification with your chartered accountant before filing your income tax return.
6. Store the exemption order, DPIIT certificate, ITR copies and audit reports safely.

Documents and details usually needed: DPIIT recognition certificate, certificate of incorporation, PAN, financial statements, audit reports and a clear note on your business activity.

Example: A two-year-old software startup in Pune with DPIIT recognition wants exemption on this year's profit. It checks the eligibility window in the notification, applies through the IMB route, and asks its CA to attach the approval while filing. A similar startup without DPIIT recognition cannot take the same route.

## Deadline

No deadline is stated for these notifications. Income tax filing follows the normal annual calendar. Check the official portal for the latest rules.

Verify these things officially before you act: your DPIIT recognition status, the exact eligibility window in the notification that covers you, and whether your business activity qualifies. If any detail is unclear, ask your chartered accountant and confirm on startupindia.gov.in.
summary: DPIIT, under the Ministry of Commerce & Industry, issues income tax exemption notifications for DPIIT-recognised startups through the Inter-Ministerial Board route. Recognition, IMB approval and correct documents are needed before you can claim anything.

title: EPFO Update: Details Not Available in the Official Source
content:
## What Happened

An EPFO announcement was expected, but the full press release is not out yet. There is no circular number, no order date and no amount or figure to report. Nothing here confirms any rule change for your Provident Fund.

This matters to every salaried employee with a UAN and an EPF account, and to EPS pension members. Your PF is long-term money. A wrong action — early withdrawal, stopping contributions, skipping KYC — can cost you interest and tax benefits. So wait for the exact official wording before you act.

## What You Can Do

1. Do not act on forwarded WhatsApp or social media claims about PF.
2. Wait for the circular or press release to be published.
3. Read the exact wording on epfindia.gov.in or on [India.gov.in](https://India.gov.in).
4. If a claim names a change, search those same words on the EPFO website. No match means no truth.
5. Still unsure? Ask your employer's HR or payroll team, or your regional EPFO office.

## Key Points

- No EPFO announcement is confirmed yet. No date, number or figure is public.
- No facts have been added here beyond what is officially confirmed.
- Check epfindia.gov.in or [India.gov.in](https://India.gov.in) for updates.
- Avoid acting on unverified messages about your PF account.
- Your own passbook is the fastest way to know where your money stands.

## How to Check Your PF Status Yourself

You do not have to wait for news to see the truth. Your own account shows it.

Details you need ready:

- Your UAN — a 12-digit number linked to your PF account.
- Your UAN password, or the OTP sent to your registered mobile number.
- Aadhaar, PAN and bank account details, kept updated as KYC.

Steps:

1. Go to the EPFO member portal and log in with your UAN and password.
2. Open the passbook view to see month-wise credits.
3. Check that both your share and your employer's share appear.
4. Look at the interest credited for the financial year.
5. Note any month where the deposit is missing.

If a month is missing, ask your employer's HR or payroll team for the ECR filing details of that month. ECR means Electronic Challan cum Return. It lists the salary and PF contribution of each employee. If the reply is unclear, raise a grievance with your regional EPFO office or through EPFO's online grievance system.

Real example: your passbook shows credits for April to August but nothing for September, while your salary slip still shows a PF deduction. Ask HR for the September ECR. If the challan was filed late, the credit usually appears once the payment is processed. If HR says it was paid but the passbook stays blank for weeks, raise a grievance.

Keep your KYC updated. Seeding Aadhaar, PAN, bank account and mobile number helps claims move faster.

## Red Flags in Forwarded PF Messages

Many PF messages spread on WhatsApp lack basic proof. Run these checks before you believe one.

- No circular number and no order date.
- No link pointing to epfindia.gov.in or India.gov.in.
- A demand for money, OTP, or your password.
- Pressure lines like 'last date today' or 'apply fast'.
- Shortened or odd-looking web links.

Most EPFO changes are announced through a circular or notification. A message without one is just a claim.

Never share your OTP, UAN password, or bank details with a caller. Genuine work happens through the portal and your employer.

If a message names a change, search those same words on the EPFO website. If nothing matches, wait. Check the official portal for the latest rules.

title: SEBI Issues Remittance Advice Against Heena Khatoon in Continental Seeds Case
content:
## What Happened

SEBI issued a General Remittance Advice on 22 September 2026. It names Heena Khatoon, the proprietor of Heena Enterprises, as a defaulter. Her PAN is FGXPK5721G.

The advice relates to a recovery case. SEBI is recovering dues under Recovery Certificate No. 8876 of 2025. That recovery grows out of an investigation into how some entities traded in the scrip of Continental Seeds and Chemicals Limited.

A General Remittance Advice tells banks and other parties to send money linked to the defaulter to the market regulator. This helps SEBI recover what is owed.

## What Changes

If you hold or manage money for Heena Khatoon or Heena Enterprises, this advice applies to you. You must remit those funds to SEBI instead of releasing them to the defaulter.

The advice also puts banks and brokers on notice. Any account linked to the defaulter in this case may face a freeze or a recovery action.

This is a recovery step, not a new penalty. It follows an earlier order that already found dues payable in this matter.

## What You Need to Do

If a bank, broker or intermediary holds funds for the named defaulter, act on the remittance advice. Send the money as directed by SEBI.

The PAN in the notice is the key identifier. Use it to check whether any account you handle matches this defaulter.

Keep records of what you remit. Note the recovery certificate number, 8876 of 2025, in your papers.

If you are an ordinary investor with no link to this case, you do not need to do anything. Your own accounts and trades are not affected.

## Deadline

No deadline is mentioned in the official source.

## Steps for Banks and Brokers

Check your records for PAN FGXPK5721G and the names Heena Khatoon and Heena Enterprises.

- If you find a match, consider freezing the account to prevent any release of funds.
- Stop all withdrawals and transfers from that account.
- Remit the funds to SEBI as directed in the remittance advice.
- Quote Recovery Certificate No. 8876 of 2025 in your remittance.
- Keep a copy of the remittance proof and the advice.

If you are unsure about any step, contact SEBI through the official portal.

## For Investors in Continental Seeds and Chemicals Limited

The recovery case is against Heena Khatoon and Heena Enterprises.

It is not against Continental Seeds and Chemicals Limited.

If you hold shares in that company, your investment is not directly affected.

The case concerns trading activities in the scrip, not the company's business.

However, if any of your accounts are linked to PAN FGXPK5721G, check with your broker.

Ordinary investors with no link to the defaulter do not need to act.

title: AICTE Web Portal Login Page: What the Official Source Actually Shows
content:
## What Happened

AICTE (All India Council for Technical Education) runs a partner portal for institutes, faculty members and students. Signing in gives access to approval files, applications, profiles and records.

A sign-in screen tells you one thing only: the portal is live and working. It does not carry a scheme, a benefit, a deadline or a rule change. There is no press note or circular attached to a login heading.

So there is nothing in a login to explain as a scheme, a rule change, or an event.

Institutes, faculty and students usually sign in for approvals, applications and records. A working login means the service is running. It does not mean something new has started inside.

If you were expecting details about a scheme, a deadline, or an order, a login cannot give them. You need the written notice or circular to know what changed.

## Key Points

- The portal is the AICTE partner portal, used by institutes, faculty and students.
- It has separate sign-in routes: institute, faculty and student.
- A login screen mentions no scheme, benefit, eligibility or deadline.
- No announcement date is attached to a login heading.
- Any real update sits behind the login, or arrives as a circular — not on the sign-in itself.
- Wait for an official AICTE circular before acting on anything.

## What Institutes, Faculty and Students Usually Do Once They Sign In

A login screen is a doorway, not a notice board. It confirms the AICTE partner portal (https://portal.aicte.gov.in/aicte/app/partnerportal/enu) is running. It does not say what has changed inside.

Most people who use this portal fall into three groups:

- **Institutes** running AICTE-approved technical programmes, who come for approval-related files and records.
- **Faculty members**, who sign in to maintain their profile and link themselves to the right institute.
- **Students**, who are usually asked to sign in only when their institute tells them to, for a specific activity.

Simple steps to follow:

1. Get the exact web address from your institute. Do not rely on a forwarded link.
2. Keep your registered email ID, mobile number and the user ID your institute gave you in front of you.
3. Pick the login option that matches you — institute, faculty, or student.
4. For approval work, keep your application or file reference ready.
5. After submitting anything, note the reference or acknowledgement number.
6. Save the receipt or confirmation if the portal gives you one.

If you are unsure which login fits you, ask your institute's AICTE nodal officer first. Your college already deals with the council and will know the right route.

Most approval and admission work follows an academic year, for example 2025-26, which continues into calendar year 2026. The exact dates for any cycle come only from the written circular, never from the login screen.

**A quick example.** A faculty member gets a forwarded message saying a new AICTE scheme has opened and asks her to sign in fast. The right move is not to start filling forms. She asks the nodal officer for the circular, checks the notices section at https://www.aicte-india.org/, and acts only after she has the circular number and date.

## How to Confirm Whether a Real Change Has Been Announced

A live login screen only proves the portal works. It says nothing about a new scheme, a revised deadline, or an order. To confirm a genuine update, check the proper channels:

- Read the circulars and notices section on the AICTE main website (https://www.aicte-india.org/).
- Check the Ministry of Education website (https://www.education.gov.in/) for its own announcements.
- Ask your institute's nodal officer, who receives official communication.
- Note the circular number, date, and file before you act on it.

If nothing appears in these places, treat it as no change. Acting on a screenshot or a forwarded message can cost you a missed deadline or a wrong application.

One thing worth remembering: a login screen changes only when the portal software is updated. A rule change or a new scheme is always announced separately, in writing, with a date and a reference number. So the two are not the same signal.

For anything that matters — fees, last dates, approvals — wait for the written circular. Check the official portal for the latest rules.
summary: The AICTE partner portal is only a sign-in doorway for institutes, faculty and students; it never announces schemes or deadlines. Confirm any real change through a written AICTE circular with a number and date.

title: Central Board of Trustees (CBT): What the EPFO Source Actually Says
content:
## What Happened

The Central Board of Trustees (CBT) is the top decision-making body of the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO). It sets policy for three EPFO schemes — provident fund, pension and deposit-linked insurance.

There is no new interest rate, no rule change and no deadline here. Nothing changes in your PF account today. Your monthly contribution, your withdrawal and your transfer run as usual.

It applies to you if you are an EPF member, an EPS pensioner, or an employer covered by EPFO. If you hold a UAN and an active PF account, CBT decisions shape the rules you follow.

CBT news is often read as a rate announcement. The board discusses the yearly PF interest rate, and headlines name it. But money reaches your passbook only after the formal approval and processing steps finish. So treat a meeting headline as the start of a process, not as cash in your account.

The board also clears scheme rule changes, annual accounts, audit reports, and the fund's income and spending. Those can affect your pension, your insurance cover and how contributions are handled.

## Key Points

- CBT sets policy for EPF, EPS and EDLI.
- It applies to EPF members, EPS pensioners and covered employers.
- A recommendation is not the same as an amount credited to you.
- Claims, transfers and withdrawals are handled by your regional EPFO office.
- The board is not a helpdesk, a bank or a court.
- Meeting notices and minutes are published on the EPFO website.

## What the CBT Actually Handles

The Central Board of Trustees is the top decision-making body for EPFO. It looks after the three EPFO schemes. These are the provident fund, the pension scheme and the deposit-linked insurance scheme.

It applies to you if you are an EPF member, a pensioner, or an employer covered by EPFO.

What usually comes up there:
- Policy and rules for EPFO offices across the country.
- The yearly PF interest rate discussion. News headlines on this often name the CBT. The final call does not rest with the board alone.
- Changes to scheme rules for PF, pension and insurance.
- Annual accounts, audit reports and the fund's income and spending.
- Appointments and administrative working of the organisation.

What it is not:
- It is not a helpdesk. It does not settle your individual claim.
- It is not a bank. It does not credit money into your passbook.
- It is not a court. It does not decide disputes between you and your employer.

Your claim, transfer or withdrawal is handled by your regional EPFO office, not by the board.

## How to Track EPFO Decisions Yourself

Do not act on a headline alone. Follow the paper trail instead.

1. Check the EPFO website for CBT meeting notices and minutes.
2. Check EPFO circulars and press notes for rule changes.
3. Log in to the member portal with your UAN and password to see your passbook, KYC and claim status.
4. If a decision affects you, wait for the circular. It gives the date the change starts.

Keep these details ready: your UAN, the mobile number linked to it, your KYC (Aadhaar, PAN and bank account) and your latest passbook entry.

A simple example. A news report says the board has cleared a higher PF rate. Your passbook will not change that day. The credit shows up only after the formal approval and processing. Wait for the EPFO announcement before you assume the higher rate is live.

Read any CBT update with three questions in mind:
- What is the date of the meeting?
- Does it say "recommended" or "approved"?
- Is there a circular telling members what to do?

If the answer to the last one is no, there is nothing for you to do yet. Keep contributing as usual. Your employer's monthly deposit and your KYC stay the same.

Check the official portal for the latest rules.
summary: The CBT is EPFO's top policy body for PF, pension and insurance. It recommends and clears rules, but your passbook changes only after the formal approval steps and the EPFO circular.

title: Ayushman Bharat Completes 8 Years: 60 Crore People Now Get Rs 5 Lakh Health Cover
content:
## What Happened

Ayushman Bharat has now completed eight years. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi marked the occasion on September 23, 2026. He shared his thoughts in a post on X with the hashtag #8YearsOfAyushmanBharat.

The Prime Minister said the scheme started eight years ago with one clear idea. Every Indian should be able to get good quality healthcare at a price they can afford. He said that idea is now turning into reality for crores of families.

## Why It Matters

More than 60 crore people can now use Rs 5 lakh of health cover every year. The Prime Minister said no other country runs a health scheme this large. This cover helps you pay for hospital treatment without emptying your savings.

He said the scheme has led to record savings on medical bills. This helps poor and middle class families the most. Instead of borrowing money or selling assets during an illness, families can use their Ayushman Bharat card.

Healthcare is also reaching closer to your doorstep. Ayushman Arogya Mandirs have recorded more than 500 crore visits so far. These centres are improving primary healthcare in villages and small towns.

The Prime Minister wished all beneficiaries well on this milestone.

## Key Points

- Ayushman Bharat has completed eight years since its rollout.
- More than 60 crore beneficiaries now get Rs 5 lakh annual health cover.
- The Prime Minister called it the largest healthcare scheme in the world.
- The scheme has led to record savings on medical expenses for poor and middle class families.
- Ayushman Arogya Mandirs have crossed 500 crore visits, strengthening primary healthcare at the grassroots.

## How to Check If Your Family Is Covered

Not every family is enrolled automatically. The cover is meant for families that meet the scheme's beneficiary criteria. So check your name before you actually need a hospital.

- Keep your Aadhaar, ration card or mobile number ready.
- Open the official Ayushman Bharat portal.
- Look for the option to check your beneficiary status.
- Enter your details as asked and search.
- If your family is listed, you can get an Ayushman card made.

If your name does not show up, ask at your nearest Ayushman Arogya Mandir or your local health office. They can guide you on the next step.

The exact steps can change over time. Check the official portal for the latest rules.

## Using the Cover at a Hospital

Once your family is on the list, the cover works at hospitals that are part of the scheme.

- Choose a hospital that is empanelled, government or private.
- Carry your Ayushman card or beneficiary ID.
- Carry a photo ID such as Aadhaar, plus your ration card if you have one.
- Go to the hospital's Ayushman help desk.
- Show your card before admission, not after the bill is ready.

Treatment is meant to be cashless for the packages the scheme covers. If someone asks for money upfront, ask why and confirm at the help desk.

Not every test, medicine or procedure is part of the scheme. Ask what is covered before you agree to the treatment.
summary: Ayushman Bharat has completed eight years since it was launched. Prime Minister Narendra Modi said more than 60 crore people now get Rs 5 lakh health cover every year. He also said this makes it the largest healthcare scheme in the world. (Source: Press Information Bureau (PIB), 23 September 2026.)

title: PM Modi Pays Tribute to Rashtrakavi Ramdhari Singh Dinkar on His Birth Anniversary
content:
## What Happened

Prime Minister Narendra Modi honoured Rashtrakavi Ramdhari Singh Dinkar on his birth anniversary. He shared his tribute in a post on X on September 23, 2026. In his message, the Prime Minister bowed to the poet and remembered his contribution to Indian literature.

## Why It Matters

Mr Modi said Dinkar's poems carry feelings of public awareness and national pride. Even today, these verses bring courage, brightness and self-respect to the hearts of Indians, he said. His writings do more than enrich literature.

They also inspire deep love and dedication towards the motherland.

The Prime Minister added that Dinkar's grand personality and timeless work will keep guiding Indians for generations to come. For readers, this is a reminder that good poetry can shape how a nation thinks and feels about itself.

## Key Points

- PM Modi paid tribute to Rashtrakavi Ramdhari Singh Dinkar on his birth anniversary.
- He praised the poet's powerful verses for carrying feelings of public awareness and national pride.
- He said the poems still fill people's hearts with courage, energy and self-respect.
- He noted that Dinkar's writings both enrich literature and inspire love for the motherland.
- He said the poet's personality and timeless creations will guide Indians for ages ahead.
- The tribute was shared publicly through a post on X on September 23, 2026.

## About Ramdhari Singh Dinkar

Ramdhari Singh Dinkar is known as Rashtrakavi, meaning 'National Poet'.

He was born on 23 September 1908 in Simaria, Bihar.

His famous works include 'Rashmirathi', 'Urvashi', and 'Kurukshetra'.

He received the Padma Bhushan in 1959 for his literary contributions.

## How to Explore His Works

You can find his poetry collections in Hindi literature sections of libraries.

Many bookstores stock his books in Hindi and English translation.

Schools and colleges often include his poems in Hindi syllabi.

Reading groups can discuss his themes of courage and patriotism.

title: Apply for DPIIT Recognition on the Startup India Portal
content:
## What DPIIT Recognition Means

DPIIT recognition is an official startup status given by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade. DPIIT sits under the Ministry of Commerce & Industry. A business that gets this tag is treated as a recognised startup by the Government of India. It is not a loan, a subsidy or a grant. It is a certificate and a number you can quote in forms, tenders and funding conversations.

Think of it as an identity card for your young company. It tells banks, investors and government departments that your business is a genuine, newly formed startup.

## Who It Applies To

It is built for founders of genuinely new businesses. Applicants are normally private limited companies, limited liability partnerships or registered partnership firms. The business should be working on a product, service or process that is new, or clearly better than what already exists in the market. Age and turnover limits also apply, and these limits get revised from time to time. Confirm the current numbers on the Startup India portal before you spend days on paperwork.

Traders, shops and businesses formed by breaking up an older firm usually do not qualify. If your idea is a copy of an existing shop with a new name, expect questions.

## Why Founders Want It

Recognition opens doors to tax and compliance relaxations, easier entry into government tenders, and access to startup-focused schemes. It also gives investors, banks and accelerators a quick way to confirm that your company is a genuine startup. Many state schemes and incubation programmes ask for the DPIIT number before they even open their form.

## Step by Step

1. Register your business first. A company or LLP is registered with the MCA. Udyam registration is a separate thing for micro, small and medium units, done at udyamregistration.gov.in.
2. Create a login on the Startup India portal at startupindia.gov.in. Use the founder's own email and mobile number.
3. Fill the recognition form. You will describe your business, the problem it solves, and why it is innovative or scalable.
4. Attach the papers. Keep your certificate of incorporation, PAN, and director or partner details ready. A short write-up on your product and how it earns money helps too.
5. Submit and note the reference number. Any query reaches you on the registered email.
6. Download your recognition certificate once it is approved, and keep the number safe.

Type clean, factual answers. Long marketing lines slow down review.

## A Real Example

Two friends build a small app that helps dairy farmers record daily milk collection. They register a private limited company, get a PAN, and apply for DPIIT recognition. Later, when a state startup scheme opens, they fill in their recognition number and qualify to apply. Without that number, the form would not accept their entry.

## What To Verify Officially

Fees, processing time and eligibility limits change, and no one can promise approval. Read the current criteria carefully on the Startup India portal, and keep your Udyam details updated at udyamregistration.gov.in. Check the official portal for the latest rules.
summary: DPIIT recognition is an official startup status from the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, applied for on the Startup India portal. It is not funding, and each benefit linked to it has its own conditions.
