title: PM Modi Congratulates Mirabai Chanu on Her Silver Medal Win
content:
## What Happened

Weightlifter Mirabai Chanu won a Silver medal in the Women's 49 kg Weightlifting event. Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated her on this achievement on 23 September 2026.

The Prime Minister said her determination and consistency continue to inspire the nation. He added that India is proud of her and wished her the very best for her future.

The Prime Minister's Office (PMO) posted the message on X, the social media platform. The post praised her silver medal win and called it special.

## Why It Matters

A medal at this level is not easy to win. It takes years of training, discipline and sacrifice. When an athlete from a small town makes it big, it gives hope to lakhs of young Indians who dream of sport as a career.

Mirabai Chanu has won medals before, and this win shows her consistency. For young weightlifters, especially girls, she is proof that strength training and hard work can take you to the world stage.

Recognition from the Prime Minister also brings attention to the sport. More attention means better support, more coaching facilities and greater interest from sponsors in the coming years.

## Key Points

- Mirabai Chanu won Silver in the Women's 49 kg Weightlifting event.
- PM Narendra Modi congratulated her and said India is proud of her.
- The PMO shared the congratulatory message on X on 23 September 2026.
- The Prime Minister praised her determination and consistency.
- He also wished her success in her future competitions.

## Starting Out in Weightlifting

Most weightlifters begin close to home. A school games period, a neighbourhood gym, or a local club is often the first step.

A few practical things help a beginner:

- Train under a coach who checks your technique, not just your strength.
- Learn the movements with light weights first. Add load slowly.
- Take part in district and state competitions to get match practice.
- Keep school or college going along with training.
- Ask your coach or state association about training centres and trials near you.

Girls often hear that lifting is not for them. Mirabai Chanu's career shows the opposite. Strength training, done safely and with guidance, builds power and confidence at any age.

Selection rules, age groups and trial dates differ by state. Confirm details with your state weightlifting association.

## What the 49 kg Category Means

The Women's 49 kg is a bodyweight category. Athletes must be within the weight limit at the official weigh-in. Weigh-ins usually happen a day before the competition.

Two lifts decide the result:

- Snatch — the bar is pulled from the floor to overhead in one continuous movement.
- Clean and jerk — the bar is brought to the shoulders first, then driven overhead.

The best snatch and the best clean and jerk are added together. The highest total wins the medal. If two athletes end on the same total, tie-break rules set by the competition organisers decide the ranking.

Bodyweight categories are reviewed from time to time. Always check the current category list with the national federation before entering a competition.
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated weightlifter Mirabai Chanu on winning a Silver medal in the Women's 49 kg event. He said her hard work and steady performances keep inspiring the country. The Prime Minister's Office shared the message on social media on 23 September 2026.

title: SEBI Board Meeting on 24 September 2026: What the Press Release Says
content:
What Happened The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) held a board meeting on 24 September 2026. SEBI put out a press release about the meeting on the same day. The release is titled "Key decisions taken in the SEBI Board Meeting dated 24th September, 2026.

The text published with this release only repeats that title. It does not spell out what the decisions are.

Why It Matters SEBI is the regulator of India's stock markets, mutual funds, and listed companies. Its board meetings often lead to rule changes. These changes can affect investors, brokers, fund houses, and company filings.

So a board meeting date matters to anyone who saves or invests in the market.

But the details are missing here. You should not rely on social media posts or rumours about what was decided. Wait for SEBI's own circulars or the fuller release before you act.

If you are an investor, keep an eye on SEBI's website for updates in the coming days.

Key Points
- SEBI's board met on 24 September 2026 for a scheduled board meeting.
- A press release about the meeting was published the same day.
- The release states that key decisions were taken at the meeting.
- The list of decisions is not given in the published text.
- Check SEBI's official website for circulars and detailed updates.

## What Happens After a SEBI Board Meeting

A board meeting is the approval stage. The actual rule usually reaches you later, through a circular.

- The board approves a proposal in the meeting.
- SEBI then issues a detailed press release or a circular.
- The circular names the entities that must comply, like brokers, AMCs or listed companies.
- It also states the date the change takes effect.
- Brokers, fund houses and companies then update their forms, systems and timelines.

For an investor, the visible change may be a new form field, a different deadline, a revised fee, or a new disclosure in a document.

Until a circular comes out, treat the decision as pending. Do not change your investments based on forwarded messages.

## How to Track the Decisions Yourself

You do not need any login or fee to read SEBI's announcements. Follow these steps.

- Go to sebi.gov.in and open Media and Notifications.
- Look under Press Releases for the 24 September 2026 item.
- Then check the Circulars section, where the operative rules are listed.
- Read the circular's effective date before acting.
- Check investor.sebi.gov.in for investor-facing updates.

If your broker, mutual fund or depository participant sends a notice, that notice will usually repeat the SEBI circular reference. Use it to find the original.

For complaints about a listed company, intermediary or market practice, use SEBI's SCORES platform on the investor website. Complaints raised there carry a tracking number.

Avoid acting on screenshots or unverified posts. Only the circular states what actually changes and from when.

title: Locate an EPFO Office Near You
content:
## What Happened

EPFO runs an official office locator on its website. It helps you find the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation office nearest to you. You pick your state and district, and you get the office address. This matters when your PF work cannot be finished online.

Sometimes PF work needs a visit in person. Your UAN may be inactive. Your employer may not be depositing PF. Your KYC may be rejected. Your pension or transfer claim may be stuck. Before travelling, you must know which office handles your case. Reaching the wrong office wastes a full working day.

## Who It Applies To

- Salaried employees with an EPF account and a 12-digit UAN.
- People whose PF transfer or withdrawal claim is pending.
- Pensioners and family pensioners covered under EPS.
- Employers who file monthly ECR returns for their staff.

## What You Can Do

1. Open the EPFO website: https://www.epfindia.gov.in/
2. Use the office locator: https://www.epfindia.gov.in/locate-epfo-office
3. Select your state, then your city or district.
4. Note the office name, full address and phone number shown.
5. Call that number before travelling and confirm working hours.
6. Carry your UAN, Aadhaar, PAN, bank passbook and payslips.

For online work, log in here: https://unifiedportal-mem.epfindia.gov.in/memberinterface/

## A Real Example

Ravi works in Pune. His PF is not credited for three months. He searches the locator, finds the Pune office, calls first, and visits with his UAN, payslips and bank statement. The officer checks the ECR record and registers his grievance. If you only know your area, use a six-digit PIN code like 400025 to narrow the search.

## Key Points

- EPFO is a central government body that runs EPF, EPS and EDLI.
- The locator shows office addresses and contact numbers, state by state.
- Routine tasks like UAN activation and KYC updates can often be done online.
- A list saved in 2026 or earlier can go stale after an office shifts.
- Always carry original ID plus photocopies for verification.
- Never pay an agent for something the locator gives you free.

## A Simple Tip

Forwarded WhatsApp lists, screenshots and old printouts often carry wrong addresses and dead phone numbers. Confirm the address and number yourself before you leave home. Check the official portal for the latest rules.
summary: EPFO's office locator helps you find the nearest EPFO office by state and district, so you know exactly where to go for PF, UAN or pension work that cannot be done online.

title: DGFT Issues Trade Notice 07 on PAN Validation Services
content:
## What Happened

The Directorate General of Foreign Trade has put out a trade notice on PAN validation services. It is called Trade Notice 07. The DGFT works under the Ministry of Commerce & Industry.

The official update is shared as a PDF document. The short public note only points readers to that document.

## What Changes

The notice deals with how PAN validation services work for trade-related processes. PAN validation means checking your Permanent Account Number against official records before it is accepted.

The exact rule changes are listed inside the trade notice PDF. This short summary does not cover them, so do not assume anything before you read the full notice.

## What You Need to Do

Open the official trade notice PDF linked in this article. Read it fully if you file DGFT applications or handle import-export paperwork.

If your PAN details do not match your other documents, fix them early. Mismatched details can slow down or block your applications.

Share the notice with your customs broker, chartered accountant, or compliance team. They handle these filings for you.

## Deadline

not stated in the official release. Check the trade notice PDF for any effective date or last date.

## Where PAN Validation Applies In Trade Filings

Your PAN is the base identity for most DGFT work. It links your firm to its Importer-Exporter Code and other registrations.

Validation means matching what you typed against income tax records. If the two do not match, your application can get flagged.

Watch these common mismatch points:
- Name spelling on the PAN card differs from your GST certificate.
- Firm name changed after registration, but PAN was never updated.
- Entity type differs across PAN, bank and IEC records.
- A partner's or director's PAN used where the firm's PAN is needed.

Keep one clean set of documents ready. A scanned PAN card, GST certificate and bank proof should all show the same name.

## Correcting PAN Details Before You File

Fix the PAN record first, not the application. A wrong PAN copy will fail validation every time.

Steps to follow:
- Compare your PAN card with your GST certificate and bank records, word by word.
- If the PAN card itself is wrong, apply for a correction through the Income Tax e-filing portal or an authorised PAN service centre.
- Wait for the corrected PAN to be issued before you start a DGFT filing.
- Save the acknowledgement number and the date of correction.
- Re-check every detail in your draft application before submitting it.

If you use a customs broker or chartered accountant, send them the corrected copy. Ask them to confirm the details match before they file.

The notice sets out how DGFT will run these checks. Read it for the exact process and any transition steps. Check the official portal for the latest rules.

title: SEBI Cancels Recovery Certificate Issued to Rashesh Purohit in TV Vision Limited Case
content:
## What Happened

SEBI has cancelled a recovery certificate linked to Rashesh Purohit. The certificate number is 7475 of 2023, and it was issued on December 14, 2023. It was issued in the matter of TV Vision Limited, and Purohit was named as the defaulter.

His PAN is ADQPP1270Q. SEBI shared this news on September 24, 2026.

## What Changes

The recovery certificate was a formal tool used to recover dues from a defaulter. Now that SEBI has cancelled it, this particular recovery process comes to an end. Anyone tracking this case should note that certificate number 7475 of 2023 is no longer in force.

The cancellation applies only to this certificate and this person.

## What You Need to Do

If you are Rashesh Purohit, you should keep a copy of this cancellation notice for your records. If you are an investor or a company dealing with TV Vision Limited, this order is for your information only. You do not need to file anything or pay anything because of this notice.

For any doubt, check the official SEBI website or speak to a legal or financial advisor.

## Deadline

There is no deadline mentioned in this order. It is a cancellation notice, not an application or compliance step. not stated in the official release.

## What a Recovery Certificate Does

A recovery certificate is a collection tool. SEBI issues it after an order asks someone to pay a sum. A recovery officer then uses it to collect that money.

Under the SEBI Act, such dues can be recovered the way land revenue arrears are recovered. This gives SEBI a stronger route than a plain demand letter.

- The certificate names the defaulter and the amount to be recovered.
- It is tied to one case and one certificate number.
- Cancelling it closes the recovery route for that certificate only.

A cancellation is not a fresh finding in the main case. It only means this recovery certificate is no longer active.

Check the official portal for the latest rules.

## If You Are an Investor in TV Vision Limited

If you hold shares in TV Vision Limited, this order asks nothing from you.

- You do not need to sell, buy or transfer shares because of it.
- You do not need to file a claim, pay a fee or send a reply.
- You can still raise a grievance if you have one against the company.

Keep your own records of shareholding, dividends and any letters you send or receive.

For complaints against a listed company, use SEBI's investor grievance system or the investor portal. Quote your folio or demat details to make tracking easier.

If you ever find your own name in a recovery list, note the certificate number and date first. Then reach out using the contact details given in that order. Keep proof of any payment you make.

title: Centre to Hold National Conference on Agriculture for Rabi Campaign 2026
content:
### What Happened

The Department of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare is holding a National Conference on Agriculture for Rabi Campaign 2026. The two-day event will take place on 28-29 September 2026. The venue is the Bharat Ratna C. Subramaniam Auditorium at the NASC Complex, Pusa, New Delhi.

Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan will open the conference. State Agriculture Ministers, senior central and state officials, ICAR representatives and other partners will attend.

### Why It Matters

This meeting brings the Centre and the states to one table. Together, they will plan a joint strategy for the coming Rabi season. The aim is to raise farm production, productivity and sustainability.

It also aims to raise farmers' incomes. The talks will build on lessons from the recent Zonal Conferences on Agriculture.

The conference looks at real problems on the ground. Leaders will study state-specific priorities and practical solutions. They want better coordination between schemes and stronger delivery at the field level.

The closing session will prepare a roadmap for the Rabi season. This roadmap supports the vision of 'Atmanirbharta & Viksit Bharat' with food and nutritional security.

### Key Points

- Day 1 will hold three rounds of parallel group discussions on major themes.
- The themes cover Atmanirbharta and production growth, climate-resilient farming, and digital agriculture, infrastructure and financing.
- Topics include pulses, oilseeds, oil palm, horticulture, cotton, seeds, natural farming, soil health, farm mechanisation, marketing reforms and the PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana.
- Day 2 will discuss the Rabi weather outlook, fertilizer supply, the Digital Agriculture Mission, Farmer Registry, AgriStack and the National Mission on Edible Oils.
- State Agriculture Ministers will share their views, and the closing session will set a roadmap for the Rabi season.
summary: The Department of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare will hold a two-day National Conference on Agriculture for Rabi Campaign 2026. It will take place on 28-29 September 2026 at the NASC Complex in Pusa, New Delhi. Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan will open the event, along with State Agriculture Ministers and other officials.

title: India at UN: Health Secretary Calls for Fair Vaccine Access and Stronger Global Health Systems
content:
What Happened

On 25 September, Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava represented India at the UN High-Level Meeting on Pandemic Prevention, Preparedness and Response in New York. She told the gathering that India is committed to stronger global health security through cooperation between countries.

She shared how India handled the COVID-19 pandemic and what the country learned from it.

Why It Matters

COVID-19 showed that no single country can fight a pandemic alone. Smt. Srivastava said the lessons from that time must turn into steady investment, stronger institutions and health systems that can handle shocks. In her view, these efforts must be built on national health systems, development plans and domestic funding.

Help from other countries should add to what a nation does for itself, not replace it.

She also asked the world to treat digital public infrastructure as a global public good. During the pandemic, digital tools helped with disease tracking, vaccination, sharing information with the public, supply chains and keeping regular health services running.

Key Points

- During COVID-19, India supplied 300 million vaccine doses to around 100 countries and two UN entities.
- India also sent medical help to more than 150 countries.
- India welcomes the WHO Pandemic Agreement adopted in May 2025, but says its value depends on a fair Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing (PABS) system.
- Countries that share pathogens and biological resources must get timely access to vaccines, diagnostics, treatments and technology, while their national sovereignty is respected.
- WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus and UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed also addressed the meeting and asked countries not to become careless after COVID-19.

Leaders at the meeting agreed that community-based systems matter for early detection, tracking and communication. This helps stop new outbreaks before they spread far. Smt. Srivastava closed by saying that preparedness is a shared duty and that fairness must stay at the centre of all future pandemic work.
summary: Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava spoke at the UN High-Level Meeting on Pandemic Prevention, Preparedness and Response in New York on 25 September. She said India is ready to work with other countries to make the world safer from future pandemics. She also pushed for fair access to vaccines and medicines for countries that share their pathogens.

title: Special Campaign 6: Government's Cleanliness and Record-Clearing Drive Starts October 2
content:
What Happened

Special Campaign 6 is a Government drive to clean up offices and clear pending work. The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) is the nodal department for it. The campaign is now in its preparatory phase, which began on 16 September 2026.

The implementation phase will start on 2 October 2026 and end on 31 October 2026.

During the preparatory phase, ministries and departments named nodal officers for their campaign offices. They trained these officers on their roles. Teams reached out to field staff and listed pending references.

They chose which offices will take part in the Swachhata (cleanliness) drive. They also checked how much electronic waste needs to be disposed and fixed the procedure for that. Plans were made for better use of office space, waste-to-wealth steps, and stronger record management.

Old records to be weeded out were identified, and historical records were marked for preservation.

A second meeting with nodal officers was held to review this work. Secretary DARPG, Smt. Nivedita Shukla Verma, chaired the meeting. More than 40 senior officers joined in person, and over 800 officers joined online.

They came from over 500 locations. Together they represented 84 ministries and departments, along with their PSUs and field offices. Shri Puneet Yadav, Additional Secretary, DARPG, presented the progress of the ongoing campaign.

Many ministries and departments shared their achievements from Special Campaign 5 and their plans for Special Campaign 6.

These include the Department of Posts, Department of Financial Services, Department of Defence Production, Department of Military Affairs, Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Railways, Ministry of External Affairs, Ministry of Mines, Central Board of Direct Taxes, and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

Why It Matters

This campaign pushes government offices to finish pending work and keep their spaces clean. It also helps them throw away e-waste safely. Better record management means you may face fewer delays when you visit a government office.

Old files get removed, and important historical records get protected.

The campaign is tracked on a dedicated web portal. Every ministry and department must upload its targets on it. Awareness is being spread through print, electronic and social media.

So far, 1,039 tweets have gone out with #SpecialCampaign6. Also, 54 PIB statements have been issued.

DARPG will bring out a collection of best practices from Special Campaign 6. This will be part of the Good Governance Week 2026 activities. The Secretary, DARPG, praised the efforts of officials and asked them to take the campaign to all PSUs, autonomous bodies and field offices, making it the biggest campaign ever.

Key Points

- Preparatory phase runs from 16 September 2026 to 30 September 2026.
- Implementation phase runs from 2 October 2026 to 31 October 2026.
- You can track progress on the portal https://[scdpm.nic.in/SpecialCampaign6.](https://scdpm.nic.in/SpecialCampaign6.)
- 84 ministries and departments are taking part, and 800+ officers joined one review meeting online.
- The campaign focuses on cleanliness, clearing pending matters, e-waste disposal, waste to wealth and better record keeping.
summary: The Government has launched Special Campaign 6, led by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances. Its preparatory phase started on 16 September 2026 and ends on 30 September 2026. The main implementation phase will run from 2 October to 31 October 2026, covering cleanliness drives, e-waste disposal and clearing of pending matters.

title: PM Modi Pays Tribute to Ashok Singhal, Shares a Personal Article
content:
## What Happened

On September 28, 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid rich tribute to Shri Ashok Singhal on his birth centenary. The Prime Minister shared his thoughts through a series of posts on X (formerly Twitter) and authored a comprehensive commemorative article reflecting on Singhal's life, philosophical vision, and public contribution.

In his tribute, Prime Minister Modi highlighted Singhal's unwavering conviction, spiritual grounding, and exceptional personal simplicity. He recalled how Singhal dedicated decades to selfless social work, grassroots mobilisation, and the cultural unity of the country.

## Historical Background and Contribution

Shri Ashok Singhal (1926-2015) was a prominent social, cultural, and organisational leader who served as the international working president of the Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) for over two decades.

Born in Agra and educated in metallurgical engineering at Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Singhal chose a path of public service through the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) as a lifelong pracharak.

He played a pivotal role in the Ram Janmabhoomi movement in Ayodhya, uniting diverse socio-cultural communities and advocating for civilisational restoration across India and among the global Indian diaspora.

## Why It Matters

Prime Minister Modi's centennial tribute highlights the enduring values of ideological steadfastness, grassroots service, and social cohesion in contemporary public life. Singhal's legacy serves as a testament to organizational leadership without personal ambition, offering lessons for modern governance and social work.

The tribute was published in both English and Hindi across national platforms to reach citizens nationwide.

## Key Points

- PM Narendra Modi marked the birth centenary of Shri Ashok Singhal on September 28, 2026.
- The tribute was shared via official posts on X and a comprehensive authored article.
- Singhal was remembered for combining spiritual dedication with tireless organizational work.
- His lifelong role in cultural awakening and social unity was prominently commemorated.
- The tribute was issued simultaneously in English and Hindi for broad national outreach.

title: Good Health Is the Base of Life's Four Goals, Says PM Modi in Sanskrit Verse
content:
What Happened

On September 28, 2026, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi shared a Sanskrit subhashitam on X. A subhashitam is a short traditional verse that carries a piece of wisdom. This verse says good health is the best root for the four goals of life.

The four goals it names are Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha. The verse also says that great sages sat peacefully together and told this sacred story. The Prime Minister posted both the Sanskrit lines and their meaning for people to read.

Why It Matters

This is a simple but powerful reminder for every Indian. Dharma means doing your duty the right way. Artha means earning a living and building a stable life.

Kama means your wishes and your happiness. Moksha means ultimate freedom and peace.

But all four rest on one thing — your health. If your body and mind are not well, it is hard to work, hard to earn, hard to enjoy life and hard to grow. So the verse asks you to treat good health as your first investment.

Eat well, sleep well, move daily and get regular check-ups.

Key Points

- PM Modi shared the verse on X on September 28, 2026.
- The verse is a Sanskrit subhashitam about health and life goals.
- It calls good health the best root for Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha.
- It also says great sages sat peacefully and narrated this sacred story.
- The takeaway for you is simple: keep your health first, everything else follows.

## Turning the Verse into a Daily Routine

The verse is a nudge, not a rule book. It says your body and mind come first. Here is how that looks in daily life.

- Students: sleep on time before exams. Late-night cramming costs more than it gives.
- Office workers: stand and walk a little every hour. All-day sitting is hard on the heart.
- Parents: cook one simple home meal and eat together.
- Senior citizens: fix one date each month for a blood pressure and sugar check.

Three habits cover most of it — food, movement and sleep. Add yearly health checks once you cross 30. If a habit slips, start again the next day. Small and steady beats big and rare.

## Where to Get Basic Health Checks in India

You do not need a private hospital for routine checks. Government health and wellness centres offer basic care. They usually sit at sub-centres and primary health centres.

- Blood pressure, sugar and weight checks are often available there.
- Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY helps with hospital bills for eligible families. The government decides who qualifies and how much is covered.
- For a medical emergency, dial 112. It works across India.

Services can differ from state to state. Check the official portal for the latest rules.
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi shared a Sanskrit subhashitam on September 28, 2026. The verse says good health is the main foundation for the four goals of life. Those four goals are Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha.

title: PM Modi Pays Tribute to Lata Didi on Her Jayanti
content:
What Happened

Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid his respects to Lata Didi on her birth anniversary. He shared his tribute in a post on X on 28 September 2026. In the post, he said her divine singing talent brought glory to the nation across the world.

He said she did not just decorate India with her melodious voice. She also always encouraged every effort linked to the country's prosperity, he added. The Prime Minister said her unmatched contribution to Indian music will be remembered for generations to come.

Why It Matters

Lata Didi is one of India's most loved singers. Her voice travelled far beyond India's borders and won hearts everywhere. For many Indians, her songs are part of daily life and old memories.

The Prime Minister's tribute shows how closely art and national pride are linked in India. It also reminds you that culture can carry a country's name to the world.

- He said her singing earned India respect across the world.
- He said she backed every effort tied to the country's progress.
- He said her work in Indian music will be remembered for ages.
- The tribute was shared in a post on X on 28 September 2026.

## Her Life and Music: A Short Look

Lata Mangeshkar was born on 28 September 1929. Her singing career ran for several decades, and her voice reached listeners far beyond India.

- She recorded songs in many Indian languages, including Hindi and Marathi.
- She received the Bharat Ratna in 2001, India's highest civilian honour.
- She also received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 1989 and the Padma Vibhushan.
- She passed away in February 2022.

Her songs still play on radio, in films and at public events across the country. That is why a tribute from the Prime Minister on her Jayanti carries weight for so many people.

## How You Can Mark Her Jayanti

Her Jayanti falls on 28 September. You do not need an official event to take part. Small, personal gestures work well.

- Play her songs at home, in your housing society or at a local club.
- Ask a nearby music school or teacher to hold a short programme for students.

title: Sadhana Shrinkhla 2026: Mission Karmayogi Training Workshops to Reach Four Regions
content:
What Happened

The Capacity Building Commission is starting Sadhana Shrinkhla 2026. It is a nationwide series of regional consultative meetings. The goal is to change how government training institutes work under Mission Karmayogi.

The first meeting will be held at Vijayawada in Andhra Pradesh on 29 and 30 September 2026. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Shri N. Chandrababu Naidu will attend this first event.

Why It Matters

Today, many training institutes only run standalone courses. The plan is to turn them into strategic, competency-driven capacity building institutions. These institutes will focus on the right skills for the right role at the right time.

This matters because well-trained officials give you better public services.

More than 900 training institutes will connect on one platform called UNNATI. This will help them share courses, faculty and infrastructure easily. A feature called UNNATI Exchange will make this sharing smoother.

Ideas from these meetings will help shape the final Training Institution Transformation Framework. The whole effort supports Mission Karmayogi's goal of building skills for Viksit Bharat @ 2047.

Key Points

- Four regional workshops will be held across India under this series.
- Each workshop is a one and a half day event.
- Training institute heads and faculty, industry partners, experts and startups will take part.
- Dr. Jitendra Singh, Minister of State for Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, will be present at the workshops.
- The meetings will guide the final Training Institution Transformation Framework.

The series follows earlier consultations held through four Regional Task Forces. These include Sadhana Saptah 2026 from 2 to 8 April 2026. A National Departmental Summit on institutionalising capacity building was also held on 15 May 2026.

## What Institutes Should Bring to the Table

These are working sessions, not speech-only events. Institutes that arrive prepared get more out of them.

- Name one nodal officer who will own the follow-up.
- Match your existing courses to the roles your officers actually handle.
- List faculty members who can teach at other institutes.
- Note spare classrooms, labs, hostels or equipment that can be shared.
- Write down the two biggest skill gaps in your department.
- Carry one success story where training visibly improved service delivery.

A clear picture of what you have and what you lack makes the discussion concrete. It also helps when the Training Institution Transformation Framework is finalised.

Nomination, travel and venue details come from the organising body. Check the official portal for the latest rules.

## A Simple Example of How Sharing Works

Imagine one state training institute has a strong course on public procurement but no spare trainer.

Another institute has a good trainer but no ready course material.

On a shared platform, the two can trade. One gives the course design, the other gives the faculty. Neither has to build the same thing from scratch.

The same logic covers infrastructure. A training hall, computer lab or hostel bed that sits idle in one place can serve learners from another.

Multiply this across 900-plus institutes, and the time and money saved adds up. For a citizen, that shows up as officials who know their job better.
summary: The Capacity Building Commission is launching Sadhana Shrinkhla 2026, a nationwide series of regional meetings on training reform. These workshops will travel to four regions of India. The first one is in Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh, on 29 and 30 September 2026.

title: SEBI Passes Final Order on Adani Group Companies Over MPS Rules
content:
## What Happened

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has passed a final order in a case involving Adani Group companies. The case relates to alleged violations of Minimum Public Shareholding (MPS) rules. SEBI put the order on its website on 28 September 2026. The public note released with the order is very short. It does not list the findings, penalties, or directions.

## What Changes

This is a regulatory order, not a new rule for the general public. It closes a pending matter about how much of a listed company's shares are held by the public. The exact outcome and any penalty amount are not stated in the official release. The names of individual companies covered by the order are also not stated in the official release. Nothing in the release describes a change to how ordinary investors buy or sell shares.

## What You Need to Do

You do not need to apply for anything or submit any form. The release does not ask any action from ordinary investors. If you want the full details, read the order document on the SEBI website. For any decision about your own holdings, speak to a SEBI-registered investment adviser.

## Deadline

No deadline is given in the official source. The order is dated 28 September 2026.

## Background

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is India's market regulator, established in 1992 to protect investors and regulate the securities market. SEBI publishes every order, circular and decision on its official website, sebi.gov.in, so that each one forms part of the public record.

An order like this is part of SEBI's enforcement work — the process by which the regulator examines a matter, gives the parties involved an opportunity to be heard, and then issues a formal, reasoned decision. Depending on the order type, the outcome can involve penalties, recovery of money, restrictions on market activity, or a correction to an earlier order.

Because these documents are legal in nature, this page explains only the general meaning of the order type involved. The official text on sebi.gov.in — searchable by company name, date or case reference — remains the authoritative version, and some orders can be appealed before the Securities Appellate Tribunal.

title: PM Modi Sends Birthday Wishes to Former President Ram Nath Kovind
content:
## What Happened

Prime Minister Narendra Modi sent warm birthday greetings to former President Shri Ram Nath Kovind. He shared the message on X (formerly Twitter) on 1 October 2026.

In his post, the Prime Minister said Shri Kovind has spent many years in public life. During this time, he stayed committed to India's development. He also worked to protect the values written in our Constitution and to help the welfare of the people.

Shri Modi added that Shri Kovind served the nation with passion and simplicity. Because of this, people from all walks of life respect him. The Prime Minister ended his message by wishing him good health, happiness and a long life.

title: First PRAMAAN Certificates Handed Over: India's Forest and Wood Certification Scheme Begins
content:
## What Happened

Union Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, handed over the first PRAMAAN certificates in New Delhi on 29 September 2026. The Indian Institute of Forest Management (IIFM), Bhopal, organised the event. IIFM runs the scheme as its operating agency.

Two recipients got the first certificates. The Andhra Pradesh Forest Development Corporation (APFDC) received one for its plantations spread over 33,000 hectares. A farmer working with the Odisha Bamboo Development Agency (OBDA) received the other. Both plantations went through a detailed field and management audit before getting certified.

Senior officers from the Ministry, State Forest Departments, certification bodies and industry attended the event.

## Why It Matters

PRAMAAN helps Indian producers, exporters and forest-based businesses meet new global rules. Big international markets now ask for proof that timber is sourced responsibly and does not cause deforestation. This certificate gives you that proof.

For farmers and forest communities, the scheme works like a livelihood mission. It brings rural and tribal communities, small farmers and forest-dependent families into a clear, verifiable system. That opens the door to premium markets without piling on extra paperwork. Women Self Help Groups and small landholders who collect or process non-timber forest produce can benefit too.

The Minister said PRAMAAN supports India's journey towards Viksit Bharat @2047. It shows an India that grows economically while protecting its ecology. He urged certification bodies, state forest departments, tree growers, farmer producer organisations and industries to join in.

## Key Points

- The first PRAMAAN certificates were handed over in New Delhi on 29 September 2026.
- APFDC got a certificate for plantations covering 33,000 hectares.
- A farmer linked to the Odisha Bamboo Development Agency also received a certificate.
- The Ministry launched IFWCS in December 2023, and these certificates mark its move to field-level work.
- Certification relies on independent audits, not on self-declaration alone.
- Forest Management certification follows the Indian Forest Management Standard, part of the National Working Plan Code 2023.
- Certification bodies must be accredited by NABCB under the Quality Council of India.
summary: Union Environment Minister Shri Bhupender Yadav gave out the first PRAMAAN certificates in New Delhi on 29 September 2026. These certificates come under the Indian Forest and Wood Certification Scheme (IFWCS). A government forest corporation from Andhra Pradesh and a farmer linked to an Odisha bamboo agency received them.
important_dates: 29 September 2026 - First PRAMAAN certificates handed over in New Delhi.
December 2023 - The Ministry launched the Indian Forest and Wood Certification Scheme (IFWCS).

title: Health Ministry Staff Join Cleanliness Drive Under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
content:
What Happened
The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare held a voluntary cleanliness drive on 1 October 2026. This kind of volunteer cleaning work is called a shramdaan. The drive took place near Gate No. 3 of Kartavya Bhavan-1, Dr. Rajendra Prasad Marg, New Delhi.

Dr. Rajiv Bahl led the drive. He is the Secretary of the Department of Health Research and the Director General of the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR). Several senior officers joined him. Smt. Aradhana Patnaik is Additional Secretary and Mission Director of the National Health Mission (NHM). Dr. Rakesh Gupta is Additional Secretary and Director General of the National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO). Dr. Loveneesh G. Krishna is the Director General of Health Services (DGHS). Other officials and staff of the Ministry also took part.

Why It Matters
This drive is part of the 'Swachhata Hi Seva 2026' campaign. The campaign theme is 'Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath'. That means one day, one hour, together. The campaign wants citizens across the country to join cleanliness work.

Speaking to the media, Dr. Rajiv Bahl said cleanliness should become a steady, shared effort. He asked officials and citizens to keep their surroundings clean and healthy. Smt. Aradhana Patnaik spoke about Jan Bhagidari, which means people's participation. She said every person has a personal responsibility here. Lasting cleanliness needs action from each of us, not just from institutions.

The Ministry also spoke about the link between cleanliness and public health. Clean surroundings, responsible waste management and active citizen participation all help create healthier spaces. The Ministry shared its commitment to the goals of Swachh Bharat.

Key Points
- The drive was held near Gate No. 3 of Kartavya Bhavan-1, Dr. Rajendra Prasad Marg, New Delhi.
- It took place on 1 October 2026 under the 'Swachhata Hi Seva 2026' campaign.
- Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Secretary (DHR) and DG (ICMR), led the drive.
- Officials from NHM, NACO and DGHS joined, along with other Ministry staff.
- The campaign theme is 'Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath'.
- Leaders asked citizens to treat cleanliness as a shared, everyday duty.
summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare held a voluntary cleanliness drive, or shramdaan, in New Delhi on 1 October 2026. It took place near Gate No. 3 of Kartavya Bhavan-1 on Dr. Rajendra Prasad Marg. Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Secretary of the Department of Health Research and Director General of ICMR, led the drive along with other senior officials and staff.

title: 8 Official Government Portals for Money and Finance in India
content:
## What This Guide Covers

Eight government portals handle most money and finance work in India. They cover tax filing, PAN services, retirement savings, small savings, benefit transfers and farmer support.

Each service has one official website. This guide lists all eight, with the link, the level (Central or State) and what the portal is for. Always use the real portal for tax returns, PF claims and benefit checks.

## The 8 Portals At A Glance

1. Income Tax e-Filing (incometax.gov.in) — file your ITR, pay advance tax, check refund status, and download Form 26AS and AIS. You must link Aadhaar with PAN if you want to file a return. Most tax notices are answered here too.
2. Protean PAN Services (tinpan.proteantech.in) — the Income Tax Department's authorised PAN provider. Apply for a new PAN, correct your details, order a reprint, or track your application. Your physical card is sent after online verification.
3. EPFO Unified Member Portal — check your PF passbook, file PF withdrawal and advance claims, and update KYC. Your claim money goes to the bank account linked with your UAN-KYC.
4. eNPS (enps.nsdl.com) — open an NPS Tier-1 or Tier-2 account and manage your contributions online. NPS gives you tax benefits under Section 80CCD and stays with you when you change jobs.
5. National Savings Institute (nsiindia.gov.in) — rates and rules for PPF, NSC, SCSS and other small savings schemes. It also explains post office procedures. Check the latest rate here before you invest.
6. PFMS (pfms.nic.in) — track Direct Benefit Transfer payments like scholarships, subsidies and social security benefits. Search by bank account or application number.
7. PM-KISAN (pmkisan.gov.in) — credits Rs 6,000 a year to eligible farmer families in three instalments. It handles e-KYC, status checks, instalment history and new registration.
8. National Portal State/UT Services (india.gov.in/services/state) — links to state tax, pension, treasury and benefit portals. Use it to reach the right State department.

## Who Is Eligible

Eligibility is different for each portal. Taxpayers use the Income Tax and PAN portals, employees use the EPFO portal, and any adult can open an NPS account. PM-KISAN is only for eligible farmer families.

State finance services are for people in that State or Union Territory.

## Benefits

Each portal saves you a trip to an office. You can file returns, fix your PAN, claim your PF, open a pension account, check savings rates, trace a benefit payment and finish PM-KISAN e-KYC from your phone or computer.

## How to Apply

Register on the Income Tax portal with your PAN and Aadhaar, then file your ITR, pay tax and track refunds from the same account. Apply for PAN on the Protean portal. Log in to the EPFO portal with your UAN for balance and claims.

Open NPS on eNPS. Check PFMS with your bank account or application number. Finish PM-KISAN e-KYC at [pmkisan.gov.in](https://pmkisan.gov.in) using OTP or biometric.

Reach state services through the National Portal.

## Important Dates

The income tax return deadline is usually 31 July for non-audit taxpayers, but always confirm the current year's date on the Income Tax portal. Advance tax instalments fall due in June, September, December and March. PM-KISAN instalments arrive in windows announced by the Ministry of Agriculture.
summary: Money work in India runs through official government websites. Tax filing, PAN, PF, pension, small savings, benefit transfers and farmer support each have one real portal. This guide lists all 8 of them and tells you what each one does. (Source: Income Tax Department / EPFO, 2 October 2026.)

title: 8 Official Government Portals Every Indian Business Owner Should Know
content:
## What This Guide Covers
India runs eight main official business services online. Each one lives on a government portal. This guide lists all eight in one place, so you know exactly where to go.

Using the right portal matters. A registration done on a look-alike site is wasted effort. Many of these services are free on the official site.

## The 8 Official Portals

### 1. GST Portal (gst.gov.in)
Cross the GST threshold and you must register here. The portal takes your registration application, monthly or quarterly returns, tax payments and refund claims. Small businesses can also check GST status and download certificates.

### 2. MCA21 (mca.gov.in)
Companies and LLPs are registered here. Annual filings, director changes and DIN updates also happen here. Starting a private limited company?

You use it for name approval, SPICe+ forms and compliance certificates.

### 3. Udyam Registration (udyamregistration.gov.in)
This is the free MSME registration. Aadhaar and PAN details are checked online. The certificate is permanent, so no renewal is needed.

Registered MSMEs can access scheme benefits and priority-sector lending.

### 4. MY MSME (my.msme.gov.in)
This Ministry of MSME portal carries schemes, notifications and grievance support. You can check scheme eligibility, download forms and follow Ministry announcements.

### 5. Startup India (startupindia.gov.in)
Apply here for DPIIT recognition if you run an eligible startup. The portal also explains tax benefits and funding schemes. The recognition certificate helps with government tenders and scheme applications.

### 6. Government e-Marketplace (gem.gov.in)
GeM is the government's own online marketplace. Sellers register, complete vendor assessment and brand registration, then list products and services. Ministries, departments and PSUs buy from here.

### 7. DGFT (dgft.gov.in)
This portal is for importers and exporters. You get your IEC (Importer Exporter Code) here. You also apply for licences, use e-scrips and read trade policy notices.

### 8. State and UT Services (india.gov.in/services/state)
State-level licences sit here, such as shop licences, labour registrations and trade permits. The page links you to your own State's portal. Check it first so you apply to the correct department.

## Pick the Right Portal
- Want GST registration? Go to the GST Portal.
- Want to register a company or LLP? Go to MCA21.
- Want MSME registration? Go to Udyam Registration.
- Want DPIIT startup recognition? Go to Startup India.
- Want to sell to government buyers? Go to GeM.
- Want to import or export? Go to DGFT.
- Want State shop or labour licences? Go to the National Portal State/UT Services page.

## Key Points to Remember
- GST registration, returns and payments happen only on [gst.gov.in](https://gst.gov.in).
- Company and LLP incorporation happens through MCA21 on [mca.gov.in](https://mca.gov.in).
- Udyam registration is free and permanent. Never pay an agent for it.
- DPIIT recognition on Startup India opens up tax benefits and government tenders.
- Sellers register on GeM to bid for government purchase orders.
- Importers and exporters need an IEC code from DGFT before shipping goods.
- State licences are found through the National Portal State/UT services page.

## Important Dates
- GST returns are due monthly or quarterly. Check the due-date calendar on the GST Portal.
- MCA annual filings are due within 30 days of the AGM. Confirm this year's dates on [mca.gov.in](https://mca.gov.in).
- Startup India recognition is open all year. Scheme-specific windows are announced on the portal.

title: Official Document Services in India: 5 Trusted Portals You Should Know
content:
India issues and stores your government documents across a few trusted online portals. Your Aadhaar, PAN, driving licence, marksheets and certificates do not sit in one place. Different departments issue them, and different portals hold them.

Knowing the right portal saves you time and keeps you away from fake websites.

## What These Services Do

These 5 services cover digital storage, birth and death records, official PDFs, ministry directories and State certificates. Each one has a fixed job. You only need to pick the one that matches your work.

## The 5 Official Portals

**1. DigiLocker – your digital document wallet**
This is a government-run wallet for documents you have already been issued. You can keep Aadhaar, PAN, driving licence and marksheets in it. Documents pulled from the issuing department are treated as valid copies under the IT Act.

That means they work like the originals for most official purposes. Portal: [digilocker.gov.in](https://digilocker.gov.in)

**2. Birth and death registration – Central and State**
This listing takes you to your own State's registration system. It works under the Registrar General of India. You must register a birth or death within 21 days of the event.

Certified copies help with school admission, passports and legal work. Portal: [services.india.gov.in](https://services.india.gov.in)

**3. Government documents directory – Central**
This is a hand-picked list of government documents, policies, Acts and public papers. You can download official PDFs of schemes and guidelines here. You do not need to hunt through many ministry websites.

Portal: [india.gov.in/my-government/documents](https://india.gov.in/my-government/documents)

**4. Government web directory – Central and State**
This is the official list of central ministries, departments, State governments and UT administrations. Every entry links to that department's verified website. Use it to confirm a site is genuine before you share any details.

Portal: [india.gov.in/directory](https://india.gov.in/directory)

**5. State and UT document services – State and UT**
Here you can browse certificate services State by State. You will find ration cards, caste certificates, land records and licences listed. Each entry links to the official State portal, so your application reaches the right office.

Portal: [india.gov.in/services/state](https://india.gov.in/services/state)

## Which Portal Should You Use?

- To store documents digitally, go to DigiLocker.
- To register a birth or death, go to the NGSP services listing.
- To find official government documents, go to National Portal Documents.
- To check a ministry website is real, go to the National Portal Directory.
- To find State certificate services, go to National Portal State/UT Services.

## Key Points

- DigiLocker holds legally valid digital copies of your issued documents.
- Birth and death registration is compulsory within 21 days of the event.
- The National Portal documents section hosts official policies, Acts and scheme PDFs.
- Always confirm a ministry website through the [India.gov.in](https://India.gov.in) directory first.
- Ration cards, caste certificates and land records come through your State's portal.

## Important Dates

- Register a birth within 21 days. A late registration needs a magisterial process.
- Register a death within 21 days, as per the Registration of Births and Deaths Act.
- DigiLocker copies get updated by issuing departments as and when they issue documents. No fixed deadline applies.

title: India's Literacy Leap: How the Country Is Moving Towards Full Literacy
content:
## What Happened

India has made huge progress in literacy over the last eight decades. In 1947, only 14% of the country could read and write. Female literacy was just 8% at that time.

The literacy rate rose from 18.32% in 1951 to 74.04% in 2011. Male literacy went up from 27.15% to 82.14%. Female literacy jumped from 8.86% to 65.46%.

Urban literacy grew from 34.59% in 1951 to 84.1% in 2011. Rural literacy rose from 12.10% to 67.8%. Between 2001 and 2011, rural female literacy grew by 26%, while rural male literacy grew by 10%.

The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2025 gives the latest picture. India's overall literacy rate is now 81.1%.

In urban areas, literacy is 89% for people aged 7 years and above. It is 88% for those aged 5 years and above. Among urban residents aged 7 and above, 93.1% of males and 84.8% of females are literate.

In rural areas, literacy is 77.4% for people aged 7 and above. It is 76.4% for those aged 5 and above. Among rural residents aged 7 and above, 84.8% of males and 70.3% of females are literate.

The Ministry of Education also defines literacy in a new way. It is the ability to read, write and compute with understanding. It also covers critical life skills like digital literacy and financial literacy. A State or UT is treated as fully literate when it reaches 95% literacy.

## Who Is Eligible

ULLAS is for adults aged 15 years and above who missed formal schooling. It gives them a second chance to learn.

Volunteers who teach under ULLAS can be school teachers, civil society workers, ASHA workers or Anganwadi workers. Surveyors identify them at the district or block level.

NIPUN Bharat is for young children in the Foundational Stage, aged 3 to 8 years. The goal is for every child to pick up basic skills by Grade 2.

Other school schemes reach students in Bal Vatikas and Classes I to VIII in government and government-aided schools. PM SHRI covers students in more than 14,500 selected exemplar schools.

## Benefits

ULLAS gives adults functional literacy, numeracy and critical life skills. Learners also get lessons in digital literacy and financial literacy through the ULLAS App.

The app carries teaching and learning material in 27 languages. It works on both iOS and Android devices, so you can study on your phone.

After learning, you can appear for the Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Assessment Test (FLNAT). You then get evaluated and certified.

School schemes improve enrolment, retention and learning outcomes. PM POSHAN gives one hot cooked meal to 11.20 crore students in 10.36 lakh schools on all school days.

PM e-VIDYA brings digital, online and on-air learning together. It is expected to reach nearly 25 crore school-going children.

Higher education has also opened up. Enrolment grew from 3.42 crore in 2014-15 to 4.50 crore in 2023-24. The Gross Enrolment Ratio rose from 23.7% to 30% in the same period.

## How to Apply

For ULLAS, surveyors conduct door-to-door visits. They find out who cannot read or write and also look for people who can teach.

If you are a learner, you are then connected with a Voluntary Teacher. That teacher helps you register on the ULLAS App.

Training, orientations and workshops are held both in person and online. You then learn at your own pace using the app material.

After studying, you appear for the FLNAT. Your result is evaluated and you receive a certificate.

The source does not list any separate form or portal for joining the other school schemes mentioned here.

## Important Dates

ULLAS aims to cover 5 crore learners during 2022-27, with a financial outlay of ₹1,037.90 crore.

NIPUN Bharat was launched in July 2021 under Samagra Shiksha. It targets universal foundational literacy and numeracy by 2026-27.

Ten States and UTs declared themselves fully literate between 2024 and 2026. These are Ladakh, Mizoram, Goa, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Sikkim, Uttarakhand and Jammu & Kashmir.

NEP 2020 sets a target of 50% higher education GER by 2035. The current GER is 30%, based on 2023-24 data.

The PLFS 2025 survey figures are the latest available. The UDISE+ Report 2025-26 recorded over 24.72 crore students enrolled in schools.

The government runs ULLAS for adults who missed formal schooling and NIPUN Bharat for early learning in children. Ten States and Union Territories have already declared themselves fully literate.

title: 8 Official Education Portals in India: Where to Apply for Scholarships, Courses, Skills and Jobs
content:
## What Happened
The Ministry of Education has put together one list of the 8 official education portals in India. These portals handle scholarships, academic credits, free online courses, skills, careers and apprenticeships. The aim is simple.

You should always land on the correct official website.

## Who Is Eligible
Almost every learner can use something from this list. School students can apply for scholarships on the National Scholarship Portal. College students can open an ABC ID to store their credits.

Jobseekers, graduates and working adults can use NCS, Skill India Digital and NATS. Parents can also use the same portals to track applications and results. Each portal sets its own rules, so check the official page before you apply.

## Benefits
The National Scholarship Portal gives you one registration, one set of documents and full status tracking. Money goes straight to your bank account. The Academic Bank of Credits keeps your credits in a digital account.

You can move them between recognised institutions under the National Education Policy. SWAYAM gives you free courses from NPTEL, CEC and NCERT. Certification is optional and paid.

National Career Service links you to employers, career counsellors and training providers at no cost. Skill India Digital hosts PMKVY and other skill courses with certificates. NATS gives you real work training with a monthly stipend.

## How to Apply
For scholarships, register on [scholarships.gov.in](https://scholarships.gov.in), fill one application and upload your documents. For ABC, open your ID through DigiLocker and share it with your college. For SWAYAM, enrol during an open window and pay only if you want the exam.

For jobs and career help, sign up free on [ncs.gov.in](https://ncs.gov.in). For skills, search courses on [skillindiadigital.gov.in](https://skillindiadigital.gov.in) by sector and place. For apprenticeships, register on [nats.education.gov.in](https://nats.education.gov.in) with your study details.

For State schemes, start from [india.gov.in/services/state](https://india.gov.in/services/state) and pick your State.

## Important Dates
NSP scholarship deadlines are fixed by your institute or department every year. Check the NSP homepage for the current cycle. SWAYAM courses open in enrolment windows through the year.

Certification exams come after you finish a course. NATS apprenticeship openings follow employer vacancies, so they appear through the year.

title: 16 Official Government Portals in India: Aadhaar, PAN, EPF, Voter ID and More
content:
## What This Guide Is About

Think about the government work you do online. Updating your Aadhaar, checking your PF balance, applying for a passport, getting a driving licence - all of it happens on a website. But for every real portal, fake look-alike sites also exist.

They can trick you into paying wrong fees or sharing personal details.

This guide puts all 16 official government portals in one place. Each one comes with its correct link, the department that runs it, and what you can actually do there. Use it as your starting point so you always land on the genuine website.

## The 16 Official Portals

**1. Aadhaar - MyAadhaar (UIDAI)**
Go to [myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in](https://myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in) to update your address, mobile number or biometrics. You can also download e-Aadhaar and check your enrolment status. Most online requests need an OTP on your registered mobile.

**2. PAN services - Income Tax e-Filing portal**
The Income Tax portal handles PAN work along with tax filing. You can check your Aadhaar-PAN linking status, validate your PAN and update your tax profile. This is the official route for most income-tax work.

**3. New PAN or corrections - Protean PAN Services**
Protean, earlier known as NSDL, is the Income Tax Department's authorised PAN provider. Apply for a new PAN, fix mistakes, order a reprint or track your application here. Your physical PAN card is posted after online verification.

**4. EPF - EPFO Unified Member Portal**
EPF members log in here to see passbook balances and file PF withdrawal or advance claims. You can also update your KYC. Claim money is credited to the bank account linked with your UAN-KYC.

**5. ESIC - Employees State Insurance Corporation**
ESIC gives health and cash benefits to insured employees and their families. Employers can register and pay contributions on the portal. Workers can access e-Pehchan cards and find dispensary details.

**6. Voter ID - ECI Voters' Service Portal**
Register as a new voter, correct your details, shift your constituency or download your e-EPIC here. A Booth Level Officer verifies your application before the electoral roll is updated.

**7. Ration Card - NFSA State/UT portal page**
The NFSA page lists the official ration-card portal for every State and UT. You apply for a new card, add a family member or complete e-KYC through your own State's system.

**8. Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY - National Health Authority**
PM-JAY gives cashless hospital cover for secondary and tertiary care to eligible families. Check your eligibility, search for empanelled hospitals and download your Ayushman card here.

**9. ABHA Health ID - ABDM**
ABHA is a free 14-digit health ID. It links your health records across hospitals and labs. You verify with Aadhaar or a driving licence, and records are shared only with your consent.

**10. PMAY Urban - PMAY-U MIS**
PMAY-U helps urban families with housing through beneficiary-led construction, affordable housing partnerships and home-loan interest subsidy. The portal shows application status and city-wise project data.

**11. PMAY Gramin - PMAY-G**
PMAY-G gives money for rural housing to households identified through SECC data. You can see sanction lists, instalment status and beneficiary details by gram panchayat.

**12. Passport - Passport Seva**
This is the official channel for fresh passports, reissues, appointments and fee payment. Your documents are checked at a PSK or POPSK appointment, and police verification follows if needed.

**13. Driving Licence and Vehicles - Parivahan**
Parivahan's Sarathi and Vahan services cover learner's licences, driving licences, vehicle registration and permits across States. Most services are fully online with RTO appointment slots.

**14. DigiLocker**
DigiLocker stores government-verified digital documents like Aadhaar, PAN, RC and insurance papers. Documents pulled straight from issuing departments count as originals under the IT Act.

**15. UMANG**
UMANG is one app and portal for many central and State services, including EPFO, gas booking, PAN and DigiLocker. A single login gets you into hundreds of services.

**16. State and UT Service Directory - National Portal of India**
This directory lists official State and UT services and links to each State's own portal. It is the safest place to start when a State, not a central ministry, runs the service.

## Which Portal Should You Use?

- Update Aadhaar or download e-Aadhaar - MyAadhaar (Central)
- Link PAN with Aadhaar or file taxes - Income Tax portal (Central)
- Apply for or correct a PAN card - Protean PAN Services (Central)
- Check PF balance or file a claim - EPFO Unified Member Portal (Central)
- Register as a voter or get e-EPIC - ECI Voters' Service Portal (Central)
- Find your State's ration card portal - NFSA State/UT portals (Central and State)
- Check PM-JAY eligibility or find hospitals - [pmjay.gov.in](https://pmjay.gov.in) (Central)
- Create an ABHA health ID - [abha.abdm.gov.in](https://abha.abdm.gov.in) (Central)
- Apply for a passport - Passport Seva (Central)
- Get a driving licence or register a vehicle - Parivahan (Central and State)
- Store and share documents - DigiLocker (Central)
- Use many services in one app - UMANG (Central and State)
- Find State and UT services - National Portal State/UT Services (State/UT)

## Key Points

- Aadhaar updates and e-Aadhaar downloads happen only on UIDAI's MyAadhaar portal.
- PAN linking, validation and tax work run on the Income Tax portal and the authorised Protean PAN portal.
- EPF members check balances and file claims on the EPFO Unified Member Portal.
- Voter registration, corrections and e-EPIC are on the ECI Voters' Service Portal.
- Ration card work is State-specific, so NFSA lists the official portal for every State and UT.
- PM-JAY health cover and ABHA health IDs run on [pmjay.gov.in](https://pmjay.gov.in) and [abha.abdm.gov.in](https://abha.abdm.gov.in).
- PMAY Urban and PMAY-G handle urban and rural housing help.
- Passport and driving licence services run on Passport Seva and Parivahan.
- DigiLocker and UMANG give you one-point access to documents and many services.

## Timing to Keep in Mind

- You can do Aadhaar demographic updates online any time. Biometric updates follow UIDAI's own schedule.
- Voter roll revisions happen in special drives that the Election Commission announces through the year.
- PMAY-G and PMAY-U instalments move as per the sanction and completion milestones shown on their portals.
summary: Most government services in India run through official websites - Aadhaar, PAN, PF, voter ID, ration card, health, housing, passport and transport. This guide lists all 16 official portals in one place so you always reach the real site. Each entry tells you what the portal does and which level of government runs it.
common_mistakes: Landing on a look-alike website instead of the official portal - always check the link from this list first.
Trying to apply for a ration card on a central site, when your State runs the service.
Forgetting that most online updates need an OTP sent to the mobile number linked with your record.

Voter roll revisions happen in special drives the Election Commission announces through the year.

title: PM Modi Shares Sanskrit Verse About Six Qualities That Bring Success
content:
## What Happened

On September 29, 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi posted a Sanskrit Subhashitam on X. A Subhashitam is a short Sanskrit verse that carries traditional wisdom. This one lists six qualities: diligence, courage, patience, the capacity for action, knowledge and valour. Mr Modi said that when a person has these qualities, even divine assistance is said to come to their aid.

## Why It Matters

The verse carries a simple and powerful message. It puts your own effort first. Hard work, bravery, patience and knowledge come before any outside help.

In short, the verse tells you not to wait for luck. Build these six qualities in yourself, and support will follow. This is the kind of everyday wisdom that fits both personal and professional life.

## Key Points

- PM Modi shared the verse on X on September 29, 2026.
- The verse is a Sanskrit Subhashitam, a short piece of traditional wisdom.
- It names six qualities: diligence, courage, patience, capacity for action, knowledge and valour.
- The message is that these qualities bring divine help to a person.
- The post carries the Sanskrit verse along with a link to the tweet.

## What You Can Take Away

You do not need to read Sanskrit to get the point. The verse is a checklist for self-improvement. Ask yourself which of the six qualities you already have, and which one you need to build.

## Background

Sanskrit subhashitas are short classical verses carrying practical wisdom — duty, perseverance, good conduct — often shared publicly as inspirational messages connecting India's heritage with everyday life.

Subhashitas have been collected in classical Sanskrit literature for centuries — collections attached to works like the Panchatantra carry sayings on conduct, duty and wisdom. Their appeal lies in compression: a single verse can carry an idea that would take pages in prose, which is perhaps why they remain popular in speeches, textbooks and social media posts alike. The verses shared on occasions like this usually emphasise universal values — perseverance, health, duty — rather than anything political, and they are routinely reproduced with translations in Indian languages alongside the original Sanskrit.
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam on X on September 29, 2026. The verse names six qualities that help a person succeed in life. Mr Modi said that when these qualities are present, even divine help comes your way.

title: New CAFE Norms for Cars Notified: Stricter Fuel Economy Rules From April 2027
content:
## What Happened

The Ministry of Power has notified new Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE) norms for passenger vehicles. These rules apply to new passenger vehicles made in India or imported for sale here. They will run from 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2032.

The new rules replace the current CAFE norms. The government finalised them after talking to car makers, industry bodies, researchers and other experts.

## What Changes

- The fuel use target gets tighter every year. It moves from 3.996 litres per 100 km in 2027-28 to 3.3273 litres per 100 km in 2031-32. That is about 16.7 per cent better over five years.
- The target line is now flatter. Lighter cars get softer targets. Heavier cars must be more fuel efficient.
- The reference weight goes up from 1,082 kg to 1,229 kg. That is about 13.6 per cent more.
- The list of recognised fuel-saving technologies grows from four to twelve. Each one earns a 1 g CO₂/km concession, up to a maximum of 9.0 g CO₂/km.
- A Carbon Neutrality Factor now counts ethanol-blended petrol, biofuels and CBG. This gives car makers another way to improve their fleet score.
- Electric cars, range-extended EVs, plug-in hybrids, strong hybrids and flex-fuel vehicles get 'super credits' in fleet calculations.
- Makers can meet their targets over two-year or three-year compliance blocks. They can carry credits forward, trade them with other makers, or buy them through the Bureau of Energy Efficiency.
- Testing will happen under both MIDC and WLTP. This helps India move towards global test methods.
- Companies selling fewer than 1,000 units a year stay exempt from fleet-average targets.
- Technologies like solar reflective paints, advanced glazing and high-efficiency air conditioning get support under this framework.

## What You Need to Do

If you plan to buy a car, nothing changes for you today. These norms apply to car makers, not to buyers. Over time, you can expect more fuel-efficient and cleaner options in showrooms.

If you run an auto company, check how the yearly targets fit your product line. Look closely at the super credits, the Carbon Neutrality Factor and the compliance blocks. These can ease your burden during the shift.

## Deadline

The new norms start on 1 April 2027. They stay in force till 31 March 2032. The old CAFE norms will be replaced from 1 April 2027.
summary: The Ministry of Power has notified new Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE) norms for passenger vehicles. The rules start on 1 April 2027 and stay in force till 31 March 2032. Cars made in India or imported for sale here will have to become more fuel efficient every year.

31 March 2032: The new CAFE norms remain applicable up to this date.

title: Narendra Bhooshan Takes Charge as Secretary of Environment Ministry
content:
**What Happened**

Shri Narendra Bhooshan has assumed charge as Secretary of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC). He belongs to the 1992 batch of the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and is from the Uttar Pradesh cadre. Before this posting, he served as Secretary of the Department of Land Resources in the Ministry of Rural Development. His career in government spans more than thirty years.

**Why It Matters**

The MoEFCC looks after the country's environment, forests and climate policy. The person heading this ministry shapes rules on pollution, forest cover and climate action. So Shri Bhooshan's experience matters to every citizen who breathes the air or depends on forests.

His background cuts across many sectors. He has worked in energy, infrastructure, industry, agriculture, urban development, finance and land-resource management. He also has training in public finance, infrastructure and climate-change preparedness. This mix could help him handle both environmental protection and development needs.

**Key Points**

- Shri Bhooshan is a 1992-batch IAS officer of the Uttar Pradesh cadre.
- He served as Additional Chief Secretary for Energy, Additional Energy Source and Technical Education in Uttar Pradesh.
- He was Principal Secretary for PWD, Infrastructure and Industries Development, I.T. and Electronics, Science and Technology, and Panchayati Raj.
- He worked as Chief Executive Officer of the Greater Noida Authority.
- As a district officer, he was District Magistrate of Mathura, Firozabad and Udham Singh Nagar.
- At the Centre, he was Deputy Director General at UIDAI and Joint Secretary in the Department of Agriculture and Cooperation.
- He also served as Mission Director for National Food Security Management and as Officer on Special Duty at ITPO under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
- He holds a graduate degree in Electronics and a Master's degree in International Development Policy from Duke University, USA.

title: PM Modi Shares Sanskrit Verse About Never Giving Up on Your Goal
content:
## What Happened

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi posted a Sanskrit Subhashitam on X on October 1, 2026. A Subhashitam is a short Sanskrit verse that carries a life lesson. He shared both the original verse and its meaning with his followers.

The verse tells a story from Hindu tradition. When the gods churned the ocean, they found precious gems and also deadly poison. The gems did not make them happy, and the poison did not scare them. They did not stop until they got the nectar of immortality.

## Why It Matters

The Prime Minister said this verse carries a simple message for everyone. People who are firm and steady do not give up until they achieve what they truly want. Small wins on the way are nice, but they are not the final goal. Problems on the way are hard, but they are not the end.

This message fits students, workers, business owners, and anyone chasing a dream. You may face setbacks and you may taste small successes. The point is to keep going until the real goal is in your hands.

- PM Modi shared the verse in a post on X on October 1, 2026.
- The Subhashitam is in Sanskrit and was shared in its original form.
- The verse talks about the churning of the ocean by the gods.
- It says gems did not satisfy them and poison did not frighten them.
- The lesson is that determined people do not rest until they reach their goal.

## Background

Sanskrit subhashitas are short classical verses carrying practical wisdom — duty, perseverance, good conduct — often shared publicly as inspirational messages connecting India's heritage with everyday life.
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam on X on October 1, 2026. The verse says that strong-minded people never stop until they reach their goal. He compared them to the gods who kept churning the ocean and did not rest until they got the nectar.

title: RoDTEP Scheme Extended Till 31 December 2026: What Exporters Should Know
content:
What Happened

The Department of Commerce issued Notification No. 41/2026-27 on 30 September 2026. This order extends the Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP) scheme till 31 December 2026. The extension covers exports made by Domestic Tariff Area (DTA) units, Advance Authorisation (AA) holders, Special Economic Zone (SEZ) units, and Export Oriented Units (EOUs).

What Changes

The scheme's end date now moves to 31 December 2026. The rates and value caps stay the same as they were on 30 September 2026. You will find them in Appendix 4R and Appendix 4RE. So your refund amount per product will not go up or down during this period. The government says this step supports exporters and helps them compete fairly in international markets.

What Is RoDTEP?

The scheme refunds the taxes that sit inside the cost of your exported goods. It covers central, state and local duties, taxes and levies that were not rebated before. It also includes prior-stage cumulative indirect taxes. This helps you price your goods better in global markets.

What You Need to Do

Keep exporting as usual and claim your RoDTEP benefits. Check the rate and value cap for your product in Appendix 4R or Appendix 4RE before you file. Remember, the old rates apply because no new rates were announced. Plan your shipments for the rest of the year knowing the scheme runs till 31 December 2026.

Deadline

The extended deadline is 31 December 2026. The notification does not say what happens after that date. So if you have shipments lined up, keep them within this window to be safe.
summary: The government has extended the RoDTEP scheme till 31 December 2026. This scheme refunds the hidden central, state and local taxes that get built into exported goods. The refund rates and value caps stay exactly the same as they were on 30 September 2026.

30 September 2026: The date on which the RoDTEP rates and value caps are treated as fixed.
