title: PM Modi Asks Indians to Buy Khadi on Gandhi Jayanti 2026
content:
What Happened

On 2 October 2026, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi remembered Mahatma Gandhi on his birth anniversary. He said Gandhiji's thoughts have inspired the whole world. He added that these ideas stay useful as long as they stay connected with people.

The Prime Minister focused on Swadeshi, or buying things made in India. He said Khadi is the most important Swadeshi product. He urged you to buy at least one Khadi item on 2 October. He also asked you to feel proud when you call it Swadeshi.

Why It Matters

Khadi is spun and woven by hand in India. When you buy it, your money supports local weavers and small businesses. That is why the Prime Minister links Khadi with the Swadeshi spirit.

The message also fits the larger goal of a Viksit Bharat. Modi said he hopes Bapu's message keeps guiding society towards a better future. Buying even one Khadi product is a small step you can take on Gandhi Jayanti.

Key Points

- PM Modi paid tribute to Mahatma Gandhi on his Jayanti, 2 October 2026.
- He said Gandhiji's thoughts have inspired the entire world and remain relevant today.
- He stressed Swadeshi, with Khadi as the foremost example.
- He asked people to buy at least one Khadi product on 2 October.
- He hoped Bapu's message would keep guiding India towards a better society and a Viksit Bharat.

## Background

Khadi is hand-spun, hand-woven cloth central to India's swadeshi movement, promoted today by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC); Gandhi Jayanti on 2 October is traditionally marked with khadi and village-industry events.

title: Government Extends Deadlines Under RELIEF Scheme for Exporters Hit by West Asia Disruptions
content:
What Happened
The Department of Commerce issued Notification No. 37/2026-27 on 30 September 2026. This notification extends the timelines under Component II of the RELIEF scheme. RELIEF stands for Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation. It is a time-bound step under the Export Promotion Mission. The scheme was launched on 19 March 2026.

What Changes
Component II asks exporters to take ECGC cover for upcoming shipments to certain regions. This cover gives you 95% risk protection. You can get it through Stand Alone Policies or Whole Turnover Policies. The policy must be taken on or after 16 March 2026. The benefit covers Full Container Load, Less than Container Load and Reefer containers. Energy shipments are left out. Your premium will also not go above the pre-disruption level for the eligible period.

What You Need to Do
Check the notification for the new last dates. If you export to the Gulf or nearby West Asia, review your ECGC policy. Talk to your insurer or ECGC about your cover. Keep your shipping and policy records ready.

Deadline
The notification is dated 30 September 2026. The exact new deadlines are not stated in the official release.

## Background

The RELIEF scheme (Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products) is a Government of India initiative administered through the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) that refunds embedded central taxes and duties on exported goods, so Indian exports are not taxed like domestic trade.

When a deadline under the scheme is extended, exporters get additional time to complete shipping bills or claims. DGFT notifies every such change through public notices on dgft.gov.in — the official notice is the authoritative document, so always verify current dates there before acting.

When a deadline under the scheme is extended, exporters get additional time to complete shipping bills or claims. DGFT notifies every such change through public notices on dgft.gov.in — the official notice is the authoritative document, so always verify current dates there before acting.

title: PM KUSUM Solar Pump Subsidy 2026 30 Percent
ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
summary: Under PM-KUSUM Component B, the central government provides 30 per cent Central Financial Assistance on standalone solar agriculture pumps, and most state governments add a subsidy of at least 30 per cent. In North-East states and certain union territories, the central share rises to 50 per cent. Here is who qualifies, how much the farmer pays, and how to apply through the state implementing agency.
content:
## What the Scheme Offers

PM-KUSUM, the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan, helps farmers move to solar-powered irrigation. Under Component B of the scheme, the government supports standalone solar agriculture pumps. These are especially useful in areas where grid electricity does not reach, so farmers can irrigate their fields without depending on diesel pumps or waiting for a power connection.

The pumps run on solar photovoltaic panels. Once installed, they use sunlight to generate electricity and pump water, which reduces running costs for the farmer.

## How Much Subsidy Do Farmers Get?

For eligible standalone solar pumps in most states and union territories, the central government provides Central Financial Assistance (CFA) of 30 per cent. This is calculated on the benchmark cost or the tender cost, whichever is lower.

The state government adds a subsidy of at least 30 per cent. The remaining amount is paid by the farmer. In many cases, farmers can cover their share through a bank loan, subject to the bank's terms and the scheme conditions.

For special regions — the North-East states, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Lakshadweep, and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands — the central assistance is higher, at 50 per cent of the benchmark or tender cost, whichever is lower. The state's minimum 30 per cent share stays the same, and the farmer pays the rest.

## Pump Capacity and Progress So Far

Under the scheme norms, farmers can generally install solar pumps of up to 7.5 HP, following state implementation guidelines. The right capacity depends on the size of the land, the water requirement, the available water source, and local sunlight conditions.

The scheme has reached significant scale. As of 31 August 2026, 13,07,190 solar pumps had been approved under Component B, and 11,80,474 standalone solar agricultural pumps had been installed. PM-KUSUM as a whole targets about 34,800 MW of renewable energy capacity, with total central assistance of about Rs 34,422 crore.

## Who Can Apply

The scheme is meant for farmers, with a focus on those in rural agricultural areas that do not have grid electricity connectivity. State-specific rules apply, so eligibility, targets, and the farmer's share of the cost can differ from one state to another.

In areas with stress on groundwater, local norms for installing solar pumps must also be followed.

## How to Apply

- Step 1: Contact the department or agency that implements PM-KUSUM in your state.
- Step 2: On the national PM-KUSUM portal, check the implementing agency for your state, the eligibility rules, available targets, the farmer's share of the cost, pump capacity options, and the application process.
- Step 3: The portal also lists vendors and rate information for standalone solar pumps.
- Step 4: Confirm the latest state-specific norms before you submit your application.
- Step 5: Apply through the state implementing agency and keep the acknowledgement safe.

## Why It Matters

Solar pumps reduce the need to buy diesel for irrigation, which helps farmers manage fuel costs that move with market prices. They also make it possible to use solar power locally in remote areas, without extending electricity lines to every field.

The savings vary from farm to farm. Pump capacity, water needs, past diesel use, local sunlight, daily usage hours, and maintenance costs all affect the actual benefit. Choosing the right pump size and using water efficiently matter as much as the subsidy itself.

title: AIIA Wraps Up Two-Week Cleanliness Drive, Turns Focus to E-Waste
content:
## What Happened

The All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, finished its Swachhata Hi Seva campaign on October 2, 2026. The Department of Swasthavritta and Yoga ran the drive from September 17 to October 2, 2026. This year's theme was “Swachhata Mein Sabhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat”.

On the closing day, a campus-wide clean-up drive took place. Director Prof. (Dr.) P. K. Prajapati joined the event with other senior faculty and staff. He said cleanliness and hygiene are a shared duty. He asked everyone to make Swachhata a daily habit. Those present also took a Swachhata Pledge to keep their surroundings clean and handle waste well. Safai Mitras were honoured for their steady work in keeping the Institute clean.

A tree plantation drive was also held in the NTPC area under the “Ek Pedh Maa Ke Naam” initiative. Several deans, Dr. Raja Ram Mahto, faculty members, and scholars joined the drive.

## Why It Matters

Cleanliness is not a one-day task. When you sort your waste at home, you reduce the load that reaches landfills. The campaign showed how small habits, like home composting and skipping single-use plastic, add up over time. The tree planting drive also helps make the area greener and cooler for everyone.

Patients and their families were part of the learning too. Talks were held in hospital waiting areas on four-way waste segregation, home composting, the Reduce-Reuse-Recycle rule, and saying no to single-use plastic. If you visit a hospital, these small steps help keep the space safe for others. Shramdaan activities also covered office premises, indoor areas, and spots in and around the campus.

The Institute is not stopping here. Special Campaign 6.0 is already running and will continue till October 31, 2026. Its focus is on collecting, separating, and disposing of e-waste properly.

## Key Points

- The campaign ran from September 17 to October 2, 2026, at AIIA, New Delhi.
- A Swachhata Pledge was taken by faculty members, scholars, and staff.
- Safai Mitras were felicitated for their regular work in keeping the campus clean.
- A plantation drive was held in the NTPC area under the “Ek Pedh Maa Ke Naam” initiative.
- Awareness sessions taught four-way waste segregation, home composting, and the 3Rs.
- Special Campaign 6.0 runs till October 31, 2026, and focuses on e-waste disposal.

The drive ran from September 17 and focused on clean surroundings, smart waste handling, and tree planting. Faculty, scholars, staff, and patients all took part in clean-up drives, pledges, and awareness sessions.

title: Two Great Indian Bustards Released Into Rajasthan's Desert National Park
content:
## What Happened

On October 4, 2026, Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav released two male Great Indian Bustards into the wild. The birds were set free at Sam, inside the Desert National Park in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan. Rajasthan's Forest and Environment Minister Sanjay Sharma attended the event, along with senior central and state officials. In a post on X, Yadav thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his guidance and support. He said the success came from nearly ten years of hard work by scientists, researchers and ground staff.

## Why It Matters

The Great Indian Bustard is a critically endangered bird. Until now, the programme focused on building a healthy breeding population in captivity. This release marks a shift towards rewilding, which means putting the birds back into their natural desert home. Learnings from this release will help refine the rules for future releases.

## Key Points

- Two male Great Indian Bustards are now free in the Desert National Park at Sam, Jaisalmer.
- The breeding centres at Sam and Ramdevra currently hold 97 birds. Of these, 40 came from eggs laid in the wild, and 57 were born in captivity.
- 86 birds stay back for breeding. 11 were marked for release, and the first 2 have now been released.
- Captive breeding produced 24 live chicks in 2025 and 29 in 2026.
- A new 'jumpstart' method placed captive-laid eggs in wild nests. Wild females accepted them, and 6 chicks hatched in Rajasthan and 2 in Gujarat.
- The Rajasthan Forest Department has fenced about 200 sq km of grassland inside the Desert National Park. WII telemetry studies call these areas prime breeding grounds.
- The Bustard Recovery Programme is run by the Environment Ministry, the Rajasthan Forest Department and the Wildlife Institute of India. The International Fund for Houbara Conservation gives technical help, and National CAMPA funds it.
- The Supreme Court's judgement guides the conservation work, based on advice from an expert committee.
summary: On October 4, 2026, Union Minister Bhupender Yadav released two male Great Indian Bustards into the wild. The birds were set free at Sam in the Desert National Park, Jaisalmer, Rajasthan. This is the first time the conservation programme has moved from breeding birds in captivity to releasing them back into nature.
important_dates: October 4, 2026: Two male Great Indian Bustards released at Sam in the Desert National Park, Jaisalmer.
2025: 24 live chicks hatched through captive breeding.
2026: 29 live chicks hatched through captive breeding.

title: UCIL Celebrates 60 Years of Uranium Mining in India
content:
What Happened
Uranium Corporation of India Limited (UCIL) has completed six decades of work. UCIL is a public sector company under the Department of Atomic Energy. It celebrated its Diamond Jubilee Year on 4 October 2026 at Jaduguda. The company was incorporated on 4 October 1967. Senior officials, scientists, engineers, workers and media professionals came together for the event.

Ms. Seema Jain, Member-Finance of the Atomic Energy Commission, was the Chief Guest. She visited the Technology Demonstration Pilot Plant at Jaduguda. She also visited the planned new site of the Dark Matter Laboratory. This lab is planned at the 815-metre level of the Jaduguda underground mine. The Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics is behind the project.

Why It Matters
UCIL mines and processes uranium. This mineral is the base resource for India's nuclear power programme. For 60 years, the company has built this capability inside India. The celebration looked back at that journey and also looked ahead.

The event opened UCIL's doors to journalists for the first time. A Journalists' Workshop was held at the Information Centre in Narwapahar. Reporters visited uranium mining and milling facilities. They got first-hand exposure to mining operations, ore handling and processing systems. A DAE Technology Exhibition showed school students how nuclear energy helps industry and society.

Dr. Kacham Anand Rao is the Chairman and Managing Director of UCIL. He said the milestone is a proud moment for every member of the UCIL family. He added that the company was glad to open its facilities to the media.

Dr Ajit Kumar Mohanty is the Secretary of the Department of Atomic Energy. He sent his greetings for the occasion. He said continued innovation and capability building matter as India moves ahead on the Nuclear Energy Mission.

Key Points
- UCIL is a public sector company under the Department of Atomic Energy.
- It was set up on 4 October 1967 and marked 60 years on 4 October 2026.
- The celebration took place at Jaduguda in Jharkhand.
- A Journalists' Workshop gave reporters direct exposure to UCIL's work.
- A DAE Technology Exhibition showed students the uses of nuclear energy.
- Ms. Seema Jain, Member-Finance of the Atomic Energy Commission, was the Chief Guest.
summary: Uranium Corporation of India Limited (UCIL) celebrated its Diamond Jubilee Year on 4 October 2026 at Jaduguda. The company was set up on 4 October 1967 and works under the Department of Atomic Energy. Ms. Seema Jain, Member-Finance of the Atomic Energy Commission, was the Chief Guest.
important_dates: 4 October 1967: UCIL was incorporated.
4 October 2026: UCIL celebrated its Diamond Jubilee Year at Jaduguda.

title: PM Modi Shares Sanskrit Verse on What Makes a Person Truly Noble
content:
What Happened

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi shared a Sanskrit verse, known as a Subhashitam, on October 5, 2026. He posted it on X, his social media account. The verse talks about the qualities that make a person truly noble.

Why It Matters

The verse lists seven qualities of a noble-hearted person. Such a person keeps a pure heart and is ready to make sacrifices. They show courage and stay calm in both happy and sad times. They are good at what they do, caring towards others, and always honest.

The verse says these are not just the habits of an ordinary friend. They are the marks of a great person with a noble heart. The post highlights these values for people to think about in their own lives.

Key Points

- The Prime Minister shared the verse on X on October 5, 2026.
- The verse is in Sanskrit and is called a Subhashitam.
- It names seven qualities: purity of heart, sacrifice, courage, calm in joy and sorrow, competence, affection, and truthfulness.
- The verse says these qualities belong to a noble-hearted and exceptional person.
- The post invites you to reflect on these values in your daily life.

## Background

The Prime Minister regularly shares Sanskrit verses on X. A Subhashitam comes from two Sanskrit words — subha, meaning good, and ashita, meaning spoken. Together they mean well-spoken words, or wise sayings that carry a life lesson. Over the years these weekly shares have become a series that many people follow and save.

The verse of October 5, 2026 focuses on the character of a noble-hearted person. It does not describe wealth or status. Instead it points to inner qualities — a clean heart, readiness to sacrifice, courage, calm in both joy and sorrow, skill in one's work, affection for others, and truthfulness. The verse presents these as the marks of an exceptional person, not ordinary habits. For readers, the post is a simple reminder to reflect on these seven qualities in daily life.
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam on social media on October 5, 2026. The verse describes the qualities of a noble-hearted and exceptional person. It says these traits go beyond being just a good friend.
important_dates: The verse was shared by the Prime Minister on October 5, 2026.

title: PM Modi Congratulates Indian Women's Golf Team on Asian Games 2026 Silver
content:
## What Happened

India's women's golf team won a Silver medal at the Asian Games 2026. The team had three players — Aditi Ashok, Pranavi Sharath Urs and Diksha Dagar.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi shared his happiness about this win. He said their success shows their strong determination and love for the sport. He also wished all three players more success in the coming years.

The Prime Minister's Office shared this message on X on October 4, 2026. The post also mentioned that the medal was won a day earlier.

## Why It Matters

Golf is still a growing sport in India. A medal at a big event like the Asian Games brings attention to the game. It also inspires young players who want to take up golf.

When the Prime Minister praises athletes openly, it tells the whole country that their hard work matters. This kind of support can help more girls and boys dream of playing for India.

## Key Points

- Aditi Ashok, Pranavi Sharath Urs and Diksha Dagar won Silver in the Women's Team Golf event.
- The event took place at the Asian Games 2026.
- PM Modi said their win reflects their determination and passion for golf.
- He wished them continued success and new heights in the future.
- The Prime Minister's Office posted the message on X on October 4, 2026.

## About the Players

The Silver medal came in the Women's Team Golf event, where national teams play together and their scores are combined for the team result. India's team comprised three golfers. Aditi Ashok is among the most experienced Indian women golfers, having represented India at the Olympic Games and at multiple Asian Games. Pranavi Sharath Urs is a younger golfer on the national circuit, and Diksha Dagar is known internationally as a deaf golfer who has competed on European tours and represented India with distinction.

Together their Silver at the Asian Games 2026 is one of India's strong showings in golf at the continental level. The Prime Minister's Office shared the congratulatory message on X on October 4, 2026, noting that the medal had been won a day earlier.

title: PM Modi Pays Tribute to Freedom Fighter Shyamji Krishna Varma on His Birth Anniversary
content:
What Happened

On 4 October 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi remembered Shyamji Krishna Varma on his birth anniversary. He paid his respects to the great revolutionary and freedom fighter. In a post on X, the PM said Varma gave his whole life to breaking the chains of India's subjugation. He also said the nation can never forget the valour Varma showed to protect the pride of the motherland. The tribute was written in Hindi on the PM's official X account.

Why It Matters

Shyamji Krishna Varma is a name many young Indians may not know well. He spent his life working against colonial rule, and a large part of that work happened far from Indian soil. His story shows you that the freedom struggle had many hands, not just a few famous names. Remembering leaders like him keeps that history alive for the next generation. It also reminds you that courage for the country can take many forms.

Key Points

- PM Modi shared his tribute on X on 4 October 2026.
- He called Shyamji Krishna Varma a great revolutionary and freedom fighter.
- The PM said Varma dedicated his entire life to ending India's subjugation.
- He said a grateful nation can never forget Varma's valour and dedication.
- The message was posted in Hindi on the PM's official X handle.

## Who Was Shyamji Krishna Varma?

Shyamji Krishna Varma was born on 4 October 1857 in Mandvi, in the Kutch region of Gujarat. He was a lawyer, a scholar and a revolutionary. After his legal studies, he studied Sanskrit and other subjects, and became known as a powerful speaker against British colonial rule.

In 1905 he founded India House in London, a hostel and centre that became a gathering place for Indian students and nationalists in Britain. He also started a journal called The Indian Sociologist, which carried strong arguments for India's freedom. Because of his revolutionary activities, the British government kept a close watch on him, and he eventually left Britain and moved to Geneva, Switzerland, where he lived until his death in 1930.

For many years his ashes remained in Geneva. In 2003 they were brought back to India and immersed in the Arabian Sea off Mandvi, his birthplace. Universities and institutions in Gujarat are named after him, and every year on his birth anniversary leaders remember his contribution to the freedom struggle.
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid homage to revolutionary and freedom fighter Shyamji Krishna Varma on his birth anniversary. In a post on X, the PM said Varma gave his life to free India from the chains of subjugation. He also said the nation can never forget Varma's courage and dedication.
important_dates: 4 October 2026 – PM Modi shared his tribute on X on Shyamji Krishna Varma's birth anniversary.
